evaluation_method: a four-configuration ablation over a 13-setup matrix of NACA 0012 airfoil and de Laval nozzle cases across three solvers and three RANS models, 340 runs, scored on execution rate and accuracy against published experimental data
baseline: the ChatCFD architecture re-implemented on Gemini, plus a standard vector RAG naive baseline
reported_result: 51% accuracy against 26% for the baseline, a 96% relative improvement; execution rate 81%; reflection rounds cut from 22.11 to 9.06
maturity_claimed: This architecture offers a scalable, auditable paradigm for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in broader industrial automation.
author_stated_limitations: the authors break down the 49% of failing cases as 10% semantically misaligned but runnable, 32% simulation-halting errors terminating on divergence or unphysical results with root cause ambiguity, and 7% exceeding the reflection threshold, and conclude that the bottleneck is no longer model capability but the density and structure of the domain-specific knowledge base

title: Advancing Subsurface Discovery and Geothermal Monitoring with an Agentic Artificial Intelligence Framework
authors: Randy Harsuko; Zhen Bi; Chen, Guodong; Rie Nakata
task: assistance and automation across geothermal field development - knowledge retrieval, inverse-algorithm discovery and automated seismic monitoring
base_model: Gemma4-26B-A4B-IT, with CodeGemma for visualisation code and Gemini 3.1 as judge
tools_used: OpenEvolve, ObsPy-based seismic routines (STA/LTA and an ML phase picker, Geiger location, Richter magnitude, ETAS forecasting), CodeGemma-generated Plotly code and a LanceDB vector store over 5,000+ papers
evaluation_method: a RAGAS-generated geothermal QA benchmark judged by Gemini 3.1, a synthetic fracture-network inverse problem comparing GAIA plus AlphaEvolve against AlphaEvolve with a fixed prompt over 10 runs, and qualitative walkthroughs of four seismic monitoring tasks
baseline: Gemma 3 and Gemma 4 without RAG; vanilla AlphaEvolve with a fixed prompt; an initial naive random-search inverse algorithm
reported_result: combined score 0.6532 against 0.6491 for AlphaEvolve and 0.6142 for the initial algorithm; up to 1.5x improvement in response accuracy and 3.1x in faithfulness on the QA benchmark
maturity_claimed: GAIA represents a pioneering application of agentic RAG workflows in geothermal field development.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state GAIA plus AlphaEvolve did not optimize the evaluator, that the fracture-network problem under-represents real world scenarios, and that the distinguishing feature is not higher accuracy of the underlying algorithms but the autonomous orchestration

title: Evaluating a 4B open-weights local LLM for agentic DFT workflows: a literature reproducibility audit
authors: Shambhu Bhandari Sharma
task: fully local agentic pipeline extracting DFT parameters from literature, translating them into SIESTA inputs and driving relaxations to convergence to audit reproducibility
base_model: qwen3:4b open weights, run locally via Ollama on an RTX 3050 Laptop and a Tesla T4
tools_used: SIESTA 5.4.2 with ONCVPSP/PSML pseudopotentials, the OpenAlex API, PDF parsers, Pydantic validation and a read-only allow-list of tools with programmatically bound arguments
evaluation_method: a corpus audit of 57 first-principles studies of pentagonal 2D materials, with the extractor scored against 201 hand-labelled expert judgements and published lattice constants recomputed
baseline: none external; comparisons across hardware and quantisation configurations and against expert hand labels and published values
reported_result: mean absolute relative error of 2.3% on 8 matched lattice-constant comparisons; extractor 95.7% precision and 67.3% recall; only 19 of the 57 studies (33.3%) reproducible in principle
maturity_claimed: establishing that lightweight open-weights models can reliably drive autonomous agentic workflows when bounded by deterministic code gates.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that qwen3:4b possesses usable semantic competence but severe structural fragility necessitating rigid programmatic gates, that evidence grounding bounds fabrication but permits misattribution which the pipeline cannot detect, and that the Critic occasionally failed to return a schema-valid object leaving verdicts unreviewed

title: Metaopenfoam: An Llm-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Cfd
authors: Yuxuan Chen; Xu Zhu; Hua Zhou; Zhuyin Ren
task: generating and running complete OpenFOAM cases from natural-language requirements alone
tools_used: OpenFOAM 10 solvers and Allrun scripts, LangChain with a FAISS vector store over OpenFOAM tutorials and command documentation, ParaView
evaluation_method: a self-proposed benchmark of eight natural-language CFD tasks derived from OpenFOAM tutorials, n=10 runs each, with five metrics and ablations removing the Reviewer role, the review-architecture action and RAG
baseline: none external; ablated variants of itself scoring 27.5%, 70% and 0% pass@1
reported_result: pass@1 rate of 85%, average executability 3.6, each test case costing $0.22 on average
maturity_claimed: MetaOpenFOAM is revolutionary
author_stated_limitations: the authors state MetaOpenFOAM cannot directly recognise data requiring secondary calculation such as Reynolds number, that for complex geometries and boundary conditions natural language inputs alone are insufficient so human participation is needed, and that similarity match may fail due to inaccurate user requirements or an inadequate database

title: AutoB2G: Agentic Simulation and Reinforcement Learning for Spatio-Temporal Grid-Interactive Building Control
authors: Borui Zhang; Nariman Mahdavi; Subbu Sethuvenkatraman; Flora Salim
task: translating natural-language task descriptions into executable building-grid co-simulation workflows and running them
tools_used: CityLearn V2, Pandapower, OpenDSS, EnergyPlus for custom dataset generation, Stable-Baselines3 SAC and PPO, and a DAG-organised internal Python codebase
evaluation_method: control-strategy experiments on 8 and 20 buildings across two low-voltage networks, plus 15 natural-language simulation tasks at three complexity levels scored on execution success rate, configuration correctness and simulation validity across three LLMs and three ablations
baseline: SOCIA without agentic retrieval and SOCIA without refinement, plus a no-control baseline and a CityLearn rule-based controller
reported_result: the full model with Claude Sonnet 4.5 reaches 1.00 execution success rate at all three complexity levels and 0.87 configuration correctness on complex tasks; ablated without-refinement variants fall to 0.33
maturity_claimed: Our results further highlight the potential of agentic LLMs as orchestration layers for scientific simulation in energy systems.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the framework has so far been implemented and validated within a limited set of platforms primarily CityLearn V2, that the primary reason for failures lies in the high degree of coupling among cross-module dependencies, and that task descriptions often exhibit a certain degree of ambiguity

title: AI CFD Scientist: Toward Open-Ended Computational Fluid Dynamics Discovery with Physics-Aware AI Agents
authors: Nithin Somasekharan; Rabi Pathak; Manushri Dhanakoti; Tingwen Zhang; Ling Yue; Andy Zhu; Shaowu Pan
task: open-ended CFD discovery - ideate, run and physically verify OpenFOAM experiments, modify solver source and write up
tools_used: OpenFOAM driven through Foam-Agent, case-local C++ library compilation with wmake, mesh generation, PyVista/matplotlib visualisation, vision-language-model image inspection of flow fields and literature retrieval
evaluation_method: five tasks run end to end under a matched GPT-5.5 backbone, scored by manual artifact inspection against two AI-scientist baselines, plus a planted-failure ablation of the verification gates
baseline: ARIS and DeepScientist at matched LLM cost
reported_result: lower-wall skin-friction RMSE against DNS reduced by 7.89%, from 0.004297 to 0.003958, on the periodic hill at Re 5600 after 44 discovery iterations
maturity_claimed: the first to span literature-grounded ideation, validated execution, vision-based physics verification, source-code modification, and figure-grounded writing within a single inspectable workflow
author_stated_limitations: the authors state all numbers use a single backbone, that no automated CFD-paper rubric scores these workflows so cross-framework comparison is manual, and they include an appendix titled What AI CFD Scientist Does Not Yet Do Well; they conclude the framework is supervised scientific assistance, not unattended publication

title: Foam-Agent: A Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Automating Computational Fluid Dynamics Workflows
authors: Ling Yue; Nithin Somasekharan; Zhang, Tingwen; Yadi Cao; Chen, Zhangze; Di, Shimin; Shaowu Pan
task: turn a single natural-language prompt into a complete, running OpenFOAM case
base_model: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B embeddings
tools_used: OpenFOAM solvers, blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, Gmsh/gmshToFoam, Allrun scripts and Python visualisation, exposed as MCP tools consumable by Cursor and Claude Code
evaluation_method: FoamBench - 110 Basic-tier and 16 Advanced-tier end-to-end OpenFOAM tasks - scored by execution success rate and bucketed field-level NMSE fidelity, with ablations on retrieval, dependency ordering and the reviewer loop
baseline: MetaOpenFOAM
reported_result: 88.2% execution success on the 110 Basic-tier tasks and 62.5% on the out-of-distribution Advanced tier, 1.6x and 5x the prior MetaOpenFOAM framework
maturity_claimed: These results show how strategic harnessing of specialized multi-agent systems can reduce expertise barriers while preserving the rigor of solver-based simulation workflows.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that errors bypassing the FatalErrorIn macros - mpirun option errors, decomposePar configuration failures and bare floating-point-exception traces - fall outside the error extractor, that closed-loop geometry modification is left to an extension, and that the external-mesh pathway is scoped to the Gmsh format

title: Towards fully automated city operations: Integrating agentic AI with urban digital twins
authors: Haowen Xu; Sisi Zlatanova; Xueping Li; Mónica Wachowicz; Michael Batty
task: a conceptual framework for agentic AI-driven urban digital twins that would select, configure and run existing urban simulation and optimisation software
tools_used: none actually called by the authors; named as invocable in principle are EnergyPlus, OpenStudio, Modelica, AutoBEM, VISSIM, SUMO, HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, EPA SWMM, Gurobi, Cesium, QGIS and PostGIS
evaluation_method: none - a vision paper with a literature review, a conceptual framework, four illustrative use cases and a research agenda
baseline: none
reported_result: none - no numeric result is reported anywhere in the paper
maturity_claimed: agentic digital twins have the potential to evolve into a central operating system for smart cities
author_stated_limitations: the authors list knowledge gaps and AI hallucination, limited data and tool access because many key tools are proprietary and do not comply with FAIR principles, lack of explainability, unclear accountability in autonomy, contextual memory limits for large simulation outputs, and risks of over-automation of critical services

title: VASPilot: MCP-Facilitated Multi-Agent Intelligence for Autonomous VASP Simulations
authors: Jiaxuan Liu; Zhu, Tiannian; C. Ye; Fang Zhong; Hongjie Weng; Quansheng Wu
task: take a natural-language materials-science mission and carry out the corresponding VASP DFT calculations end to end
tools_used: VASP, pymatgen for input generation and output parsing, a Slurm scheduler, the Materials Project structure database, Python plotting and a Flask web interface
evaluation_method: demonstration missions - band structure and density of states for 2H-MoS2, plane-wave cutoff convergence tests, lattice relaxations with multiple van der Waals schemes, and cross-material band-gap comparisons
baseline: none
reported_result: no success rate or error metric is reported; the headline claim is qualitative - VASPilot completed the missions reliably and without manual intervention
maturity_claimed: an open-source platform that fully automates VASP workflows
author_stated_limitations: the authors state essentially no limitations, framing the gaps as extensions - capabilities can be readily extended through additional agents and tools, and the framework can be adapted to other DFT codes by deploying the corresponding MCP server

title: IteraSim RAG: A Multi-Stage Retrieval-Augmented Agentic Back-End for OpenFOAM-Based Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Pratyush Kumar
task: assemble runnable OpenFOAM input decks from a natural-language request via multi-stage retrieval over a curated knowledge corpus
base_model: not stated - described only as a fast general-purpose chat-tuned LLM at temperature 0, never named
tools_used: OpenFOAM icoFoam, simpleFoam, interFoam, buoyantBoussinesqSimpleFoam and MPPICFoam, plus blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, Gmsh, checkMesh, wmake, pyFoam and ParaView
evaluation_method: a 28-case benchmark scored by retrieval tag coverage, a 30-query ablation of the retrieval stages, six reference configurations run end to end on OpenFOAM v2506 with a 0-4 executability rubric, and two synthetically corrupted cases as fatal-error probes
baseline: flat single-query RAG, plus a tabulated comparison against OpenFOAMGPT, MetaOpenFOAM, FoamGPT, Foam-Agent, ChatCFD, CFDAgent and SwarmFoam
reported_result: a mean retrieval coverage of 77.9%, median 79.1%, across the 28-case benchmark, with parameter-modification cases exceeding 90%
maturity_claimed: All six reference configurations run to completion on OpenFOAM v2506, and two synthetically corrupted cases are diagnosed and repaired within the bounded Reviewer loop.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the reported 77.9% is a conservative lower bound on operational retrieval quality, that the scoring rule under-counts synonymous surface forms, that two under-covered cases are attributable to corpus-coverage gaps, that the benchmark does not exercise multi-physics regimes, and that executability-tier evidence is deferred to a companion technical note

title: Agentic Modelling Pipeline: Reproducible Rapid Stormwater Modelling Management System with OpenClaw
authors: Zhonghao Zhang; Caterina Valeo
task: configure, run, verify and plot an EPA SWMM stormwater model from a natural-language prompt with an auditable per-run manifest
base_model: GPT 5.2 as the primary model of OpenClaw version 2026.2.17
tools_used: the EPA SWMM 5.2.4 command-line engine, pysheds/rasterio/numpy for DEM pour-point detection, SWMM report and binary output parsers, and matplotlib plotting, exposed through three MCP servers
evaluation_method: three-part verification on one catchment - automatic pour-point detection against manually identified PCSWMM pour points, 120 repeatability runs across two 30-sample parameter sweeps executed both by CLI and by MCP, and identical INP files run in the SWMM GUI against the agentic workflow
baseline: manual SWMM/PCSWMM GUI configuration and direct swmm5 command-line execution
reported_result: R2 and NSE identically 1.0 across all 30 simulations, max absolute peak-flow difference 0.0, outlet peak flow 3.366 cubic metres per second with continuity errors at or below 0.003%
maturity_claimed: to the authors knowledge, this is the first time Agentic AI (OpenClaw) has been applied to peak runoff prediction
author_stated_limitations: the authors state they only encapsulated the peak flows of interest, that a lumped model representation was used for demonstration purposes, that poor prompting can lead to variability in how non-expert users specify tasks, and that the interpretability of the results does not arise from the agentic AI itself or from the underlying LLM

title: Large language model agent as a mechanical designer
authors: Yayati Jadhav; Amir Barati Farimani
task: generate and iteratively refine 2D truss structures against FEM-computed stress and mass constraints
tools_used: an in-house Python FEM truss evaluator, unnamed; the LLM emits a Python dict parsed directly into the FEM module; pymoo/NSGA-II used only for the baseline
evaluation_method: 2 tasks by 3 constraint variations by 3 temperatures by 2 model scales, 10 independent runs per configuration, max 25 iterations per run, scored on max stress, stress-to-weight ratio, iteration count and success rate
baseline: NSGA-II via pymoo at 500 and 1000 generations with population 100; Bayesian optimisation and ground structure methods attempted and reported as unsuccessful
reported_result: faster convergence and fewer FEM evaluations than NSGA-II, which needed 1000 generations at population 100 - 100,000 FEM evaluations - against a 25-iteration cap for the LLM agent
maturity_claimed: These results highlight the promise of LLM agents to function as a new class of natural language-based, reasoning-driven optimizers
author_stated_limitations: the authors state a notable limitation is difficulty producing floating-point values with high precision for continuous parameters such as nodal coordinates, that in the absence of explicit objective functions LLMs may converge slowly or terminate prematurely, and that LLMs are best positioned not as replacements for traditional optimizers but as a new class of reasoning-based design agents

title: Autonomous Traffic Signal Optimization Using Digital Twin and Agentic AI for Real-Time Decision-Making
authors: Salman Jan; Toqeer Ali Syed; Shahid Kamal (23807824); Qamar Wali; Ali Akarma
task: autonomous real-time traffic-signal timing optimisation against a continuously synchronised traffic digital twin
tools_used: an in-house traffic-network digital twin for what-if simulation, a Feature Store, an MCP Gateway, traffic management APIs and a secure message bus
evaluation_method: simulation study on a synthetic 12-intersection urban grid across three scenarios - light traffic, heavy traffic and an incident partially blocking a road - tabulated against two baselines
baseline: a Fixed-Time controller with a 60-second cycle and a reinforcement learning adaptive controller trained on six months of traffic data
reported_result: flow efficiency 85% against 80% for RL and 75% for fixed-time; average vehicle delay 49 s against 54 s and 60 s, an 18% reduction over fixed-time control
maturity_claimed: The present work uniquely combines all three components - digital twin, agentic AI with LLM-driven reasoning, and MCP-secured action execution - into a unified, compile-ready operational framework.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that operating in the wild raises concerns regarding variability and reliability of sensor data, communication delays in congested cities, and regulatory concerns over fully autonomous traffic signal control, and that future research will involve pilot testing and connection with real infrastructure APIs

title: LLM Agent for Fire Dynamics Simulations
authors: Lu Xu; Danyal Mohaddes; Yi Wang
task: make FireFOAM fire-dynamics CFD usable by natural language - source-code insight, case configuration and job submission
tools_used: a shell command tool including the fireFoam executable and scontrol, a Python interpreter tool, a retrieval tool over the FireFOAM C++ source, and SLURM on an AWS ParallelCluster
evaluation_method: seven unambiguous single-correct-outcome tasks across code insight, case configuration and job execution, each repeated five times, judged by comparing the agent actions to an experienced FireFOAM user
baseline: none
reported_result: 5/5 on the four low-complexity tasks, 4/5 on running a serial job, 1/5 on HPC job submission and 2/5 on the multi-functionality task
maturity_claimed: proof-of-concept
author_stated_limitations: the authors state a robust ability for optional human feedback was not achieved due to technical challenges with the chosen agentization framework, that asynchronous simulation running requiring state save and recovery was not addressed, and that the experiments considered only GPT-4o

title: TO-Master: an LLM-agent framework for automated topology optimization
authors: Haoju Lin; Wenchang Zhang; Weipeng Xu; Xiang Lorraine Li; Tian Xu; Tianju Xue
task: turn finite-element topology optimisation into a natural-language, tool-orchestrated workflow
base_model: not stated - no LLM is named anywhere in the paper
tools_used: MCP-exposed JAX-FEM tools for mesh generation, boundary-condition visualisation, 2D and 3D topology optimisation with and without stress constraints, thermal topology optimisation, and image-to-geometry conversion
evaluation_method: eleven worked cases plus an instruction-ablation study of 6 reference runs and 120 fuzzy-prompt runs, scored by a two-stage protocol - a boundary-condition checker then expert review against the reference solution
baseline: none externally; four prompt-ablation variants are internal comparisons
reported_result: 96.7% success rate under the full instruction with fuzzy prompts, against 83.3% without chain-of-thought, 73.3% without few-shot and 40.0% without tool-usage constraints
maturity_claimed: TO-Master removes the burden of trivial setup and routine model construction, lowers the modeling barrier of TO, and preserves a reliable numerical workflow.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the ablation study is limited to six regular benchmark cases, that users may need to inspect the previewed supports, loads and passive domains before optimisation, that the system assumes a self-consistent unit system, and that broader industrial benchmarks and standardised quantitative metrics are needed

title: OpenFOAMGPT: A retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) agent for OpenFOAM-based computational fluid dynamics
authors: Sandeep Pandey; Ran Xu; Wenkang Wang; Xu Chu
task: set up, modify and run OpenFOAM CFD cases from natural language, including boundary-condition changes, turbulence-model swaps and cross-distribution code translation
base_model: GPT-4o and o1-preview, with o1-mini in the zero-shot table
tools_used: OpenFOAM-v2406 solvers icoFoam, simpleFoam, buoyantBoussinesqSimpleFoam, interFoam, MPPICFoam and pimpleFoam, with case dictionary editing and a RAG database of tutorial descriptions
evaluation_method: five evaluation blocks - zero-shot setup of six tutorial cases, few-shot with RAG scored on iterations, tokens and cost, alternate boundary conditions and mesh resolution, turbulence-model addition, and code translation between OpenFOAM distributions
baseline: the same agent without RAG, comparisons across GPT-4o, o1-mini and o1-preview, and a web-based LLM without the agent for code translation
reported_result: with RAG the agent successfully sets up all tested cases; $0.03 to $0.36 per scenario with GPT-4o and up to $1.60 with o1; execution under ten minutes in each instance
maturity_claimed: our results underscore the agent's potential to significantly streamline or even automate advanced CFD tasks with minimal human input
author_stated_limitations: the authors state a measure of human oversight remains critical to ensure correctness, and that fluctuations in model performance over time mean users must carefully monitor updates for mission-critical or high-precision applications

title: Modular large language model agents for multi-task computational materials science
authors: Akshat Chaudhari; Janghoon Ock; Amir Barati Farimani
task: route natural-language materials-science queries to database retrieval, continuum simulation, crystal-structure generation or molecular dynamics
tools_used: the Materials Project API via pymatgen, MatWeb scraping, CrystaLLM for CIF generation, a cellular automata tool, a Monte Carlo annealing tool, and ASE-based molecular dynamics with the EMT potential
evaluation_method: eleven qualitative case studies across four task types plus a reliability analysis - 10 independent runs of a materials-extraction prompt scored by intersection over union, 5 runs each for three continuum prompts, and 10 runs of an MD prompt scored on agent selection, parameter extraction, tool invocation, execution, output format and content accuracy
baseline: vanilla gpt-3.5-turbo side by side
reported_result: parameter extraction 100% success across five runs and materials extraction consistent in 9 of 10 runs; MD reliability 100% on agent selection, parameter extraction, tool invocation and execution, 80% on output format
maturity_claimed: the system shows the stability required for materials research
author_stated_limitations: the authors state LLMs alone are inherently limited in delivering rigorous scientific predictions for complex physical phenomena, that one run failed to extract any material IDs suggesting an isolated error, and that broadening data sources and enabling the agent to write or adapt code would increase flexibility

title: El Agente Quntur: A research collaborator agent for quantum chemistry
authors: Juan B. Pérez-Sánchez; Yunheng Zou; Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo; Marcel Müller; Ignacio Gustín; Andrew Wang; Han Hao; Tsz Wai Ko; Changhyeok Choi; Eric S. Isbrandt; Mohammad Ghazi Vakili; Hanyong Xu
task: plan, execute, adapt and analyse computational quantum-chemistry experiments end to end by driving the ORCA package
tools_used: the full ORCA 6.0 feature set including DFT, coupled cluster, NEB, IRC, GOAT and excited-state dynamics, plus GFNn-xTB relaxation, Python and Bash execution, PDF-to-Markdown conversion and ChimeraX visualisation
evaluation_method: a new benchmark of 17 computational quantum chemistry exercises spanning undergraduate to research level, each executed autonomously five times and graded by expert human graders against per-question rubrics, plus open-ended research-level case studies
baseline: none formally; the predecessor El Agente Q is compared architecturally
reported_result: per-question average scores over 5 repetitions are reported in figures; one case study confirms agreement with experimental results within chemical accuracy, below 1 kcal per mol
maturity_claimed: These two major advances bring Quntur to the category of research collaborator
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that LLMs struggle with more complex geometry-related tasks, that the most significant limitation arises during geometry generation for transition-state searches, that geometric reasoning is currently a major bottleneck for AI agents in chemistry, and that in one case study most transition-state results are likely incorrect

title: Aether: Network Validation Using Agentic AI and Digital Twin
authors: Jordan Augé; Sam Betts; Giovanna Carofiglio; Giulio Grassi; Martin Gysi; John Kenneth d'Souza
task: validate proposed network configuration changes against a network digital twin before deployment
tools_used: Batfish model-based verification, a custom NS-3 flow-level simulator, RouteNet performance prediction, Diffy anomaly detection, an ArangoDB knowledge graph, and NETCONF/OpenConfig device access
evaluation_method: 8 synthetic network change scenarios with expert-built ground truth plus 2 reproduced production incidents from a major ISP, scored on classification precision, error detection, LLM-judged correctness, consistency, robustness, coverage, redundancy and time to answer
baseline: none directly comparable; compared qualitatively against traditional CI/CD pipelines and manual lab testing
reported_result: 94% error detection and 64% precision in synthetic benchmarks, and 100% detection with 73% precision in production environments; coverage 92-96%; average execution time about 6 minutes per run
maturity_claimed: Aether demonstrates practical value for autonomous network operations, serving as an intelligent assistant for routine validation while operators focus on strategic decisions.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state a small subset of challenging queries causes the majority of failures, that the test executor agent's main failure mode is misuse of network digital twin tool parameters, that ground truth creation requires iterative expert validation, and that guardrails and agent monitoring are next steps toward production-grade autonomy

title: Text-to-flowsheet: an LLM-assisted pipeline for expert-level digitization and automated simulation of chemical processes
authors: Jan-Frederic Laub; Luca Bosetti; André Bardow
task: convert natural-language descriptions of chemical production processes into flowsheet graphs and converged Aspen Plus simulations
tools_used: Aspen Plus reached by automated translation of the flowsheet graph, thermodynamic property calculations, and black-box optimisation of unit parameters
evaluation_method: benchmark against 101 hand-collected expert-drawn flowsheets for 30 chemical production processes, comparing graph similarity of LLM output to experts against pairwise expert-to-expert similarity
baseline: 50 chemical engineering experts, as a pairwise expert-expert flowsheet similarity distribution
reported_result: for most processes the median similarity of LLM-generated flowsheets to expert flowsheets lies within the distribution of pairwise expert similarities
maturity_claimed: For the first time, we demonstrate that an automated pipeline can achieve expert-level accuracy in process topology digitization.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the main limitation of digitizing flowsheets from textual descriptions is incomplete information about the chemicals, processing steps and operating conditions, and that a significant challenge is the propagation of errors from LLM-based digitization to the final Aspen simulation

title: SwarmFoam: An OpenFOAM Multi-Agent System Based on Multiple Types of Large Language Models
authors: Chunwei Yang; Yankai Wang; Jianxiang Tang; Haojie Qu; Ziqiang Zou; Yi Liu; Chunrui Deng; Zhifang Qiu; Ming Ding
task: drive OpenFOAM CFD simulations end to end from natural-language and image inputs
base_model: Gemini-2.5-flash for the main tests and DeepSeek-Chat in the head-to-head with Foam-agent
tools_used: OpenFOAM-9 with blockMesh, checkMesh, Allrun and seventeen named solvers, ParaView via pvpython, and a local RAG knowledge base of six OpenFOAM help documents
evaluation_method: 25 independent test cases - 10 natural-language and 15 multimodal - scored on iterations, token usage, pass rate and cost, plus ablations removing multi-modal pre-parsing and the error-correction agent, plus three validation cases
baseline: Foam-agent, both using DeepSeek-Chat, on the 10 natural-language cases
reported_result: overall pass rate 84% across 25 cases - 80% natural language and 86.67% multimodal; token consumption 83.85% lower than Foam-agent; removing the error-correction agent reduced pass rate by 60%
maturity_claimed: successfully realizing intelligent CFD proxy
author_stated_limitations: the authors state general-purpose LLMs still exhibit unreliability when constructing complex geometries and generating meshes, struggling with curved boundaries and unstructured grids, that configuration errors accounted for 71.1% and 44.9% of errors in the multimodal and natural-language tests, and that future work needs simulation validation criteria rather than judging correction need from log errors alone

title: PDEFlow: Autonomous Agentic PDE Pipelines for Neural Operator Learning and Solver-Free Inference
authors: Akshat Jani; Prathamesh Gadekar; Sakhinana Sagar Srinivas; Venkataramana Runkana
task: turn natural-language ODE and PDE descriptions into validated solver configurations, generated datasets and trained neural operators
tools_used: a FEniCSx finite-element backend, a JSON specification validator, a patch repairer, an operator registry and a shared neural-operator training interface
evaluation_method: 70 scripted ODE and PDE scenarios - 15 ODE, 30 one-dimensional PDE and 25 two-dimensional PDE - run through the agent graph with the generated JSON specification compared against a reference specification
baseline: three ablations - no repairer, no validator, and a single-shot baseline
reported_result: the complete system achieves the highest aggregate accuracy at 81.43%
maturity_claimed: The framework is designed for repeatable scientific and engineering workflows where many related physics configurations must be specified, simulated, learned, and queried with minimal manual intervention.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that operator selection is still manual, that the solver backend is currently limited to one- and two-dimensional rectangular domains with linear PDEs, and that support for nonlinear PDEs would require nonlinear residual assembly

title: TSAgent: An Agentic Workflow for Autonomous Transition State Search
authors: Varun Madhavan; Ankit Mathanker; D Sweeney; Oluwatosin A. Ohiro; Yixin Wang; Bryan R. Goldsmith
task: autonomous transition-state search for heterogeneous catalysis at density functional theory level
tools_used: VASP 6.3 for DFT, ASE 3.26.0 for structure preparation and NEB path interpolation, SLURM job submission on an institutional HPC cluster, convergence diagnostics, expert-crafted debugging guidelines and a replan log
evaluation_method: a 100-example subset of the OC20NEB heterogeneous catalysis benchmark scored for success, a 10-example held-out comparison against human experts, and a 12-catalyst reproduction of published Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi scaling relationships
baseline: a human-expert average of 73 plus or minus 12 percent and a universal interatomic-potential baseline
reported_result: an overall success rate of 83% on the benchmark with a 95% Wilson confidence interval of 74.5 to 89.1 percent, and 70% on held-out examples against a human-expert average of 73 plus or minus 12 percent
maturity_claimed: TSAgent independently reproduces Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi scaling relationships for NH3 dissociation on metal and single-atom alloy surfaces from a published heterogeneous catalysis study, demonstrating that its utility extends beyond curated benchmarks to real scientific investigations.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state LLM-based verification is not a physical guarantee and automated transition-state assignments accepted without human oversight could propagate errors into downstream mechanistic conclusions, that the workflow assumes reasonable reactant and product geometries are provided, and that the evaluation is restricted to 100 of the 600 available reactions

title: Engineering.ai: A Platform for Teams of AI Engineers in Computational Design
authors: Ran Xu; Yupeng Qi; Feng, Jingsen; Xu Chu
task: teams of role-specialised AI engineers running coupled aerodynamic, structural, acoustic and optimisation computational design workflows
tools_used: FreeCAD for CAD, Gmsh for meshing, OpenFOAM simpleFoam for CFD, CalculiX for finite element analysis, a Python Brooks-Pope-Marcolini acoustic model and Docker-based parallel execution
evaluation_method: a UAV wing optimisation case study - twelve CFD cases over four NACA airfoils at Reynolds numbers 1e5 to 1e6, 432 structural configurations through the FreeCAD-Gmsh-CalculiX pipeline, coupled with acoustic analysis
baseline: none
reported_result: a 100% success rate across over 400 parametric configurations, with zero mesh generation failures, solver convergence issues, or manual interventions required
maturity_claimed: This work demonstrates that agentic-AI-enabled AI engineers have the potential to perform complex engineering tasks autonomously.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that API rate limits highlight the mismatch between parallel computational workflows and sequential API processing, and that privacy and intellectual property concerns arise when transmitting proprietary design specifications to external APIs

title: DREAMS: Density Functional Theory Based Research Engine for Agentic Materials Simulation
authors: Ziqi Wang; Haiming Huang; Hancheng Zhao; Changwen Xu; Shang Zhu; Jan Janßen; Venkatasubramanian Viswanathan
task: autonomous DFT materials simulation - convergence testing, lattice-constant and adsorption-energy workflows under a verification guard
base_model: Claude Sonnet 4.5 for supervisor and workers at temperature zero, Claude Opus 4.8 for the safety-guard judges
tools_used: Quantum ESPRESSO, AutoCat for adsorption-site identification, ASE for structure representation and input preparation, SLURM job submission and monitoring, a convergence-diagnosis agent and provenance-checking tools
evaluation_method: three periodic DFT benchmarks - the 27-element Sol27LC lattice-constant dataset, the CO on Pt(111) adsorption-site puzzle, and Bayesian ensemble uncertainty quantification
baseline: MDCrow and ChemGraph, prior agentic simulation frameworks
reported_result: average errors below 1% on the Sol27LC lattice-constant benchmark
maturity_claimed: DREAMS operates at an enhanced L2 (L2+) automation level and demonstrates capabilities approaching L3 automation, providing a path toward trustworthy, high-throughput autonomous materials simulation.
author_stated_limitations: the authors report recurrent failures including loss of task history, disregard of convergence results, attempts to bypass tool refusals, incorrect arithmetic, reduced verification during extended executions and circumvention of provenance checks, including one case where an unsupported value was passed through the identity x+0 to produce a valid provenance record without validating the original value

title: CFDAgent: A language-guided, zero-shot multi-agent system for complex flow simulation
authors: Xu, Zhaoyue; Wang, Long; Wang, Chunyu; Chen, Yixin; Luo, Qingyong; Yao, Hua-Dong; Wang, Shizhao; He, Guowei
venue: 中国科学院力学研究所
task: run end-to-end CFD simulations of flow past generated geometries from a natural-language or image prompt
tools_used: Point-E text-to-3D diffusion, GLIDE image generation, Marching Cubes, signed-distance-function regression, an immersed-boundary flow solver and postprocessing scripts
evaluation_method: reproduction of canonical sphere flows at Reynolds numbers 100 and 300 from three input modes - text prompt, image and standard sphere model - with drag and lift coefficients compared to published values
baseline: published reference data from Johnson and Patel (1999), Fadlun et al. (2000) and Kim et al. (2001)
reported_result: drag and lift coefficients from each input mode closely match available data, for example a drag coefficient of 0.68 at Reynolds number 300 against a literature value of 0.66
maturity_claimed: Through extensive tests on canonical and realistic scenarios, we demonstrate the robustness, versatility, and practical applicability of CFDagent.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the limited quality and controllability of the generated geometries hinder precision, and that performance is constrained by the inherent complexity of CFD simulations, leading to significantly prolonged processing times

title: Self-Refining Topology Optimization via an LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework
authors: Hyunjee Park; Hayoung Chung
task: autonomously formulate, code, run and self-refine density-based topology optimisation problems
base_model: not stated for the agents; GPT-5.4 Thinking is used only as the single-pass baseline
tools_used: FEniCS for finite element analysis, pyOptSparse with SNOPT as the optimiser, and generated Python scripts run by a non-LLM executor agent
evaluation_method: 10 independent sessions each on three benchmark topology optimisation problems - cantilever compliance, MBB compliance and L-shaped stress minimisation - scored by success rate
baseline: GPT-5.4 Thinking as a single-pass single-LLM baseline
reported_result: success rate improved from 80% to 100% on the MBB variant and from 10% to 80% on the L-shaped stress-minimisation problem, over 10 trials per problem
maturity_claimed: In such cases, the proposed framework reliably produces converged designs where a single state-of-the-art LLM struggles.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that less commonly documented formulations such as stress minimisation with constraint aggregation are handled by conditionally adding references to the runtime context, and that three-dimensional topology optimisation and integration with manufacturing process parameters remain open directions

title: GENIUS: An Agentic AI Framework for Autonomous Design and Execution of Simulation Protocols
authors: Soleymanibrojeni, Mohammad; Aydin, Roland; Guedes-Sobrinho, Diego; Dias, Alexandre C.; Piotrowski, Maurício J.; Wenzel, Wolfgang; Rêgo, Celso Ricardo Caldeira
task: turn free-form natural-language requests into valid, self-debugging Quantum ESPRESSO DFT input files that run to completion
base_model: Mixtral-8x22b, DBRX, Llama-3.1-405b, Claude-3.5-Sonnet and Gemini-2.0-Flash
tools_used: Quantum ESPRESSO pw.x v7.2, a smart QE knowledge graph, Materials Cloud structure databases, ASE and a FastAPI REST interface
evaluation_method: 295 free-form calculation prompts contributed by independent researchers, each translated to a QE input, executed and scored on whether pw.x ran to completion, with per-attempt success decay curves
baseline: base LLMs prompted directly without the GENIUS framework
reported_result: input files run to completion on about 80% of 295 diverse benchmarks, of which 76% are autonomously repaired
maturity_claimed: GENIUS delivers incremental efficiency gains while enabling a fundamental shift in how - and by whom - materials discovery can be conducted
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that improving the knowledge graph, particularly the connections and conditions, remains future work, and that the present knowledge graph covers only pw.x so extending it to other Quantum ESPRESSO modules and codes beyond QE would broaden reach

title: Hierarchical Multi-agent Large Language Model Reasoning for Autonomous Functional Materials Discovery
authors: Samuel Rothfarb; Megan C. Davis; Ivana Matanović; Baikun Li; Edward F. Holby; Wilton J. M. Kort-Kamp
task: LLM-driven active-learning search of a transition-metal chemical space for target adsorption energies, designing and running the DFT calculations itself
base_model: GPT-5 via the OpenAI Agents SDK, with Codex v0.57.0 invoked as a subprocess for structure-building code
tools_used: VASP as the DFT engine, the ASE library for structure construction, the Codex CLI as a code-writing subprocess and version-controlled directories for candidate archiving
evaluation_method: four reasoning strategies benchmarked over 28 transition metals in two model systems, 100 independent runs per target energy window, with cumulative success probability and Shannon-entropy analysis of exploration
baseline: random sampling, a Monte Carlo agent and a deliberately randomising rogue agent
reported_result: reasoning-driven exploration reduces required atomistic simulations by up to 90% relative to trial-and-error selection
maturity_claimed: multi-agent collaboration accelerates materials discovery and marks a new paradigm for autonomous scientific exploration
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that in small fully enumerable spaces such as their adatom benchmark the implicit calibration is sufficient, but that in larger or less well-characterised domains an additional retrieval-augmented agent would be needed to supply prior grounding

title: Harnessing AtomisticSkills for Agentic Atomistic Research
authors: Bowen Deng; Bohan Li; Matthew Cox; Hoje Chun; Juno Nam; Artur Lyssenko; Sathya Edamadaka; Jurgis Ruza; Xiaochen Du; Nofit Segal; Jesus Diaz Sanchez; Mingrou Xie
task: equip a general-purpose coding agent with curated atomistic-simulation skills so it can run computational materials and chemistry campaigns
base_model: not stated - compatible hosts named but not which model produced the reported results
tools_used: VASP, atomate2, ASE, pymatgen, RDKit, MACE, FairChem, MatGL, OpenMM, AutoDock Vina and the Materials Project, QMOF and ARC-MOF databases
evaluation_method: text-mining 500 npj Computational Materials articles, LLM decomposition of each into required skills and computation of the fraction covered by the skill library, plus case-study campaigns on solid-state electrolyte conductivity and virtual screening
baseline: literature-reported values for the electrolyte conductivities and the DUD-E benchmark with published AutoDock Vina results
reported_result: covers 56.2% of computational materials skills usage on average across 500 sampled papers; DUD-E CDK2 area under curve 0.70
maturity_claimed: AtomisticSkills provides a critical agent infrastructure towards building fully autonomous AI scientists.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the framework functions predominantly in a co-pilot modality where human researchers provide high-level directives, and that human supervision remains critical to guide the agent through complex multi-day scientific workflows

title: AutoDFT: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations
authors: Penghui Yang; Zhonghan Zhang; Yue Li; Xinrun Wag; Yanchen Deng; Yuhao Lu; Bijun Tang; Zheng Liu; Bo An
task: plan, run, monitor and repair end-to-end VASP DFT workflows from a natural-language task description
base_model: GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
tools_used: VASP, vaspkit, VASP parameter and INCAR generation and log parsing
evaluation_method: VASPBench, 34 DFT tasks derived from the official VASP documentation, scored for end-to-end task success, plus property accuracy against a 20-material Materials Project subset and an ablation isolating the closed loop
baseline: a rule-based hand-crafted-template pipeline and an open-loop variant with a single LLM planning call
reported_result: 94.1% task-level success, 32 of 34, with GPT-5.2, against 82.4% open-loop and 67.6% rule-based
maturity_claimed: By closing the loop between planning and execution, AutoDFT enables experimentalists without deep computational expertise to obtain reliable first-principles results.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that closed-loop adaptation remains useful even when the initial planner is strong since several successful runs still depend on recovery or plan modification, and that the scope excludes energy above hull, advanced optical excitations, transport coefficients and full phonon dispersions

title: Towards Fully Automated Molecular Simulations: Multi-Agent Framework for Simulation Setup and Force Field Extraction
authors: Marko Petković; Vlado Menkovski; Sofı́a Calero
task: extract force-field parameters from the literature and assemble runnable RASPA adsorption-simulation input decks from a natural-language request
tools_used: RASPA, file-manipulation tools, file-content extraction functions and literature force-field sources
evaluation_method: each simulation-setup task repeated five times, with the resulting input files inspected manually and executed in RASPA, scored by success rate and execution rate across single-structure and 500-structure zeolite tasks
baseline: none
reported_result: high success and execution rates per task - 100% on single-structure tasks and 80 to 100% on 500-structure tasks; no single headline number is stated in prose
maturity_claimed: highlighting this approach's potential to enable fully autonomous, scalable materials characterization
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that knowledge is encoded procedurally in prompts and tools, limiting the ability of agents to adapt across tasks or refine strategies based on past experience

title: Empowering Scientific Workflows with Federated Agents
authors: Alok Kamatar; J. Gregory Pauloski; Yadu Babuji; Ryan Chard; Mansi Sakarvadia; Daniel Babnigg; Ian Foster; Kyle Chard
task: middleware for deploying and coordinating long-lived autonomous agents across federated HPC, instrument and data resources
base_model: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct in the case studies; Academy itself is model-agnostic
tools_used: Globus Compute and Parsl executors, Globus Auth, ProxyStore, Redis, the LAMMPS GPU library, CP2K, ML generation and screening models and instrument control interfaces
evaluation_method: microbenchmarks of agent startup, action latency and weak scaling on Aurora, Polaris and Chameleon Cloud compared against other actor runtimes, plus four application case studies
baseline: Dask Actors, Ray Actors, the AutoGen distributed runtime and Globus Compute
reported_result: starts 3,328 actors in 7.6 seconds and achieves 3.4K actions per second maximum throughput on a single agent
maturity_claimed: This framework enables scalable and flexible orchestration of intelligent agents across heterogeneous resources.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that LLMs combined with tool calling cannot currently construct complex real-world science applications, with frequent problems including improperly configured or invoked codes that ran without errors but produced incorrect results, and that permissions are currently coarse-grained

title: Deploying Frontier Agentic Technology in MOOSEnger, a Multiphysics-Capable AI Assistant
authors: Zaid Abulawi; Mengnan Li; Guillaume Giudicelli; Yang Liu; Cody Permann
task: write, validate, repair and run MOOSE multiphysics finite element input files from a natural-language prompt
tools_used: MOOSE input checking and execution, the MOOSE Language Server Protocol, MOOSE documentation and example retrieval, LangGraph and Mem0
evaluation_method: a 200-prompt benchmark spanning eight physics categories, where a prompt counts as successful when the generated input runs and matches the requested physics, geometry, boundary conditions and outputs, plus a worked IAEA hexagonal-duct case compared to a reference model
baseline: ChatGPT 5.2 standalone at 5% success and Gemma 4 31b standalone at 0%
reported_result: 179 of 200 prompts, 90%, with GPT 5.2 and 153 of 200, 76.5%, with Gemma 4 31b, against standalone baselines of 5% and 0%
maturity_claimed: moving toward fully capable, locally-hosted agents for MOOSE-based multiphysics modeling
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that closing the remaining gap in the harder categories is a natural next step, through category-specific retrieval, expanded skills and refined instructions

title: Battery-Sim-Agent: Leveraging LLM-Agent for Inverse Battery Parameter Estimation
authors: Jiawei Chen; Xiaofan Gui; Shikai Fang; Shengyu Tao; Shun Zheng; Weiqing Liu; Jiang Bian
task: inverse estimation of physical battery-model parameters by LLM-guided fitting against a simulator
base_model: GPT-O3, with ablations on GPT-OSS 120B and Qwen2.5
tools_used: the PyBaMM Doyle-Fuller-Newman simulator for forward runs on proposed parameter vectors, with Meta Ax used for the Bayesian optimisation baseline
evaluation_method: a 200-task simulated benchmark over five chemistries in Regular and Extreme modes plus real-world CALCE battery tasks, scored by curve-matching MAPE and RMSE under an iteration budget of 80
baseline: Bayesian optimisation, CMA-ES and published default parameters
reported_result: 67 to 95% reduction in curve-matching error compared to traditional black-box optimization baselines
maturity_claimed: Our results highlight the promise of LLM-agents as reasoning-based optimizers for scientific discovery and battery parameter estimation.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the agent behaviour is inherently probabilistic and tighter theoretical characterisation of convergence remains open, that classical Bayesian optimisation remains competitive in low-headroom chemistries, and that simulator edge cases remain difficult for all methods because the forward PyBaMM model itself becomes numerically unstable

title: LARA: Validation-Driven Agentic Supercomputer Workflows for Atomistic Modeling
authors: William Dawson; Louis Beal; Yoann Curé; Giuseppe Fisicaro; Dorian Rolland; Luigi Genovese
task: generating and validating atomistic-simulation workflows for execution on supercomputers
base_model: Gemini 2.5 Flash as the stage-specific model and Sonnet 4.6 as the frontier model
tools_used: BigDFT via the remotemanager package, MCP tools served with FastMCP, dry-run tool calls for execution-level verification and retrieval over BigDFT training material
evaluation_method: two demonstration tasks - atomization enthalpy and surface adsorption energies on a 291-atom titanium dioxide slab - run through the four-phase pipeline on Fugaku, with qualitative reporting of detected API misuse and physically inconsistent configurations
baseline: none
reported_result: resource-planning numbers only, such as about 1.2 GB of headroom per process on the worst-case calculation
maturity_claimed: The results show that validation-driven generation significantly improves robustness and enables iterative correction of both syntactic and physical inconsistencies.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the implementation realises the pipeline only up to the validation phase and that the critical review phase is not implemented end to end

title: AutoSurrogate: An LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous Construction of Deep Learning Surrogate Models in Subsurface Flow
authors: Jiale Liu; Nanzhe Wang
task: autonomous construction, training and deployment of deep-learning surrogate models for subsurface flow
base_model: not stated - candidate families named but no specific model, and all inference is performed on a locally deployed model
tools_used: Optuna Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, PyTorch training and checkpointing, data-profiling and GPU-memory-estimation utilities and diagnostic failure-detection tools
evaluation_method: a 3D geologic carbon storage case with 1,000 SGeMS realizations simulated in GEOS, with surrogate accuracy compared against eight hand-designed architectures and three AutoML methods
baseline: UNet3D, ResUNet3D, RecurrentRUNet3D, Encoder-Decoder ConvLSTM, CNN-Transformer, U-DeepONet, FNO3D and U-FNO, plus Random Search, Optuna TPE and Hyperopt TPE
reported_result: pressure R2 of 0.9976 and CO2 saturation R2 of 0.9532, outperforming the best baseline at 0.9359 by 1.73 percentage points
maturity_claimed: the proposed framework establishes a new paradigm for surrogate modeling, shifting from manual and heuristic workflows to automated, scalable, and intelligent model construction
author_stated_limitations: there is no limitations section; the authors note only that residual errors concentrate near the plume boundaries where the saturation field changes rapidly

title: NVAITC AI Scientist: A Governed End-to-End Research System -- A Hypertension GWAS Case Study
authors: Eddie Huang; Ken Ying-Kai Liao; Iven Fu; Yang-Hsien Lin; Chao-Shun Zhan; Andy Liao; Virginia Chen; Johnson Sun; Pika Wang; Richard Huang; Jiun-Cheng Jiang; Ting-Yuan Liu
task: governed end-to-end execution of institutional biomedical analysis workflows under privacy constraints
tools_used: a Broker v2 API for SQL extraction, cohort materialization, GWAS and polygenic-risk-score pipelines and job launch and polling, plus PLINK2 and Kubeflow Pipelines on Kubernetes
evaluation_method: a single-institution hypertension GWAS case study on a hospital cohort, with agent-derived phenotype labels and outputs compared against independently curated expert phenotypes and analyses
baseline: independently curated expert-led analyses
reported_result: the strongest signal at FGF5 reaching minus log10 p of about 70, from a cohort of 286,422 individuals
maturity_claimed: These results demonstrate that governed agentic research systems can support scalable AI-assisted biomedical discovery while producing scientifically reliable outputs comparable to expert-led workflows.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state it is a single-institution case study, that the GWAS results constitute replication evidence rather than novel discovery, that a dataset of this size is insufficient for clinical-grade validation of drug-induced liver injury prediction, and that comparison between agent-derived labels and expert phenotypes revealed systematic discordance

title: MatClaw: An Autonomous Code-First LLM Agent for End-to-End Materials Exploration
authors: Chenmu Zhang; Boris I. Yakobson
task: end-to-end materials exploration by writing and executing Python that orchestrates multiple simulation codes on HPC
base_model: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.0 Flash
tools_used: Python execution with pymatgen, atomate2, jobflow-remote, ASE, DeePMD-kit and phonopy, driving VASP and LAMMPS backends on remote HPC clusters, with retrieval over domain source code
evaluation_method: three end-to-end demonstrations on ferroelectric CuInP2S6 plus three multiple-choice question-answer benchmark suites comparing chunking methods, retrieval strategies and LLM providers
baseline: the no-RAG per-question error rate, which ranges from 5% to 30%
reported_result: per-step API-call accuracy of about 99% with retrieval-augmented generation, against a no-RAG per-question error rate of 5% to 30%
maturity_claimed: LLMs already handle code generation and scientific interpretation reliably, and the rapid improvement in their capabilities will accelerate materials discovery
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the agent consistently struggles with what they term tacit domain knowledge, including appropriate simulation timescales, equilibration protocols and sampling adequacy for phase transitions

title: From Specification to Execution: AI Assisted Scientific Workflow Management
authors: Komal Thareja; Hamza Safri; Rajiv Mayani; Anirban Mandal; Ewa Deelman
task: generating reviewable workflow specifications and executable workflow implementations for a workflow management system
base_model: Claude Opus 4, OpenAI GPT-5.4 and Kimi K2.6
tools_used: Pegasus workflow management system for planning, data staging, orchestration, provenance and fault recovery, HTCondor job execution and the pegasus-ai skills plugin
evaluation_method: generated federated-learning medical-imaging workflows executed on a distributed HTCondor pool on the FABRIC testbed, assessed on execution success and structural quality in a 50-round experiment with 101 sub-workflows
baseline: expert manual implementation, described as taking an expert months to build
reported_result: 101 sub-workflows and 2,679 jobs on GPUs at four sites completed in two days, work described as taking an expert months to build
maturity_claimed: Production-ready means the generated workflow executed end to end on the pool of Section IV.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the evaluation covers one application and one workflow management system, and that future work will apply the methodology to other scientific workflows, workflow systems and AI coding agents to assess generality

title: Masgent: An AI-assisted Materials Simulation Agent
authors: Guanghen Liu; Songge Yang; Yu Zhong
task: natural-language preparation, construction and analysis of DFT and machine-learning-potential simulation workflows for materials
base_model: provider-selectable backends; which one produced the reported case studies is not stated
tools_used: VASP input generation with SLURM job scripts, pymatgen, ASE, Icet, the Materials Project API, and the SevenNet, CHGNet, Orb-v3 and MatterSim machine-learned potentials
evaluation_method: a workflow-preparation-speed benchmark over ten materials, a machine-learned-potential accuracy and speed benchmark against DFT references, and six case studies
baseline: manual scripting time of 1 to 3 hours per material, DFT-PBE reference calculations and literature values
reported_result: full workflows prepared for each system in under 30 seconds against 1 to 3 hours manually; machine-learned potentials deliver 1000 to 10000 times speedups relative to DFT
maturity_claimed: positioning it as a next-generation computational assistant capable of accelerating both exploratory and production-level materials simulations
author_stated_limitations: the authors state Masgent is intentionally designed to avoid autonomous decision-making in areas requiring physical judgment such as functional selection and convergence settings, that although it prepares complete workflows it does not execute VASP jobs or manage HPC queues, and that ambiguous prompts may still require user clarification

title: A status quo investigation of large-language models for cost-effective computational fluid dynamics automation with OpenFOAMGPT
authors: Wenkang Wang; Ran Xu; Jingsen Feng; Qingfu Zhang; Sandeep Raj Pandey; Xu Chu
task: natural-language setup and execution of OpenFOAM CFD cases, benchmarked across cheaper LLM backends
base_model: OpenAI o1, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen 2.5-Max and a locally deployed 4-bit quantised QwQ-32B on a single RTX 4090
tools_used: the OpenFOAM v2406 runner and its solvers icoFoam, simpleFoam, buoyantBoussinesqSimpleFoam, interFoam, MPPICFoam and pimpleFoam, with case file generation
evaluation_method: standard OpenFOAM cases run per model under zero-shot and retrieval-augmented conditions, scoring validity of generated setups plus token cost
baseline: the earlier OpenFOAMGPT built on GPT-4o and o1 with retrieval
reported_result: cost savings of up to two orders of magnitude compared to OpenAI o1, with per-case costs of roughly $0.25 to $0.67 for successful runs
maturity_claimed: the framework adeptly handles a range of flow configurations (including single- and multi-phase flow) in just a few iterations
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that locally deployed smaller models such as QwQ-32B struggled with generating valid solver files for complex processes, that zero-shot prompting commonly failed in simulations with intricate settings even for large models, and that challenges with boundary conditions and solver keywords stress the requirement for expert supervision

title: QUASAR: A Universal Autonomous System for Atomistic Simulation and a Benchmark of Its Capabilities
authors: Faqing Yang; Jack D. Evans
task: autonomous end-to-end atomistic simulation - planning, running and analysing DFT, machine-learning-potential, molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo workflows
base_model: gemini-3-flash-preview for all reported benchmark runs
tools_used: Quantum ESPRESSO for DFT, MACE machine-learned potentials, LAMMPS for molecular dynamics, RASPA3 for Monte Carlo, plus ASE and pymatgen
evaluation_method: a three-tiered benchmark suite of nine cases - routine tasks, multi-step workflows and frontier research tasks - with the top tier repeated twice for consistency
baseline: none; a capability comparison table against El Agente Quantum, DREAMS and LAMMPS-Agents rather than a head-to-head run
reported_result: CO2 in UiO-66 adsorption of 5.98 mmol/g at 298 K and 10 bar; a melting point of 928.70 K against a reference of 933.45 K
maturity_claimed: QUASAR, a production-level universal atomistic computation system
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that performance is bounded by the underlying domain knowledge of the chosen model, that LLM-induced errors often present as structurally coherent but numerically or physically unsound outputs, that the system does not support agent-driven HPC job submission, and that non-determinism affects reproducibility

title: El Agente Sólido: A New Age(nt) for Solid State Simulations
authors: Sai Govind Hari Kumar; Yunheng Zou; Andrew Wang; Jesús Valdés-Hernández; Tsz Wai Ko; Nathan Yue; Olivia Leng; Hanyong Xu; Chris Crebolder; Alán Aspuru-Guzik; Varinia Bernales
task: autonomous design, execution and troubleshooting of solid-state first-principles Quantum ESPRESSO workflows
base_model: not stated - the paper never names the LLM backbone
tools_used: Quantum ESPRESSO with SLURM submission, Phonopy, the UMA and MACE machine-learned interatomic potentials, PORMAKE framework construction, and Materials Project and OQMD database queries
evaluation_method: 7 benchmarking exercises at two difficulty levels with 10 trials each, 70 trials in total, scored against chemist-written rubrics, plus four case studies
baseline: reference calculations performed by computational chemists and experimental thermal data
reported_result: an average score of 97.9% across 7 benchmarking exercises, each repeated at least 10 times
maturity_claimed: El Agente Solido exemplifies a rapid shift toward agentic computational chemistry
author_stated_limitations: the authors state future developments will focus on expanding methodological coverage to excited-state methods, explicit solvation and finite-field approaches, that PBE pseudopotentials systematically overestimate lattice constants, that the quasi-harmonic approximation does not capture magnon-phonon couplings, and that prior work rarely evaluated consistency and reproducibility across multiple trials

title: MooseAgent: A LLM Based Multi-agent Framework for Automating Moose Simulation
authors: Tao Zhang; Zhenhai Liu; Yong Xin; Yongjun Jiao
task: automated generation, execution and correction of MOOSE multiphysics simulation input files from a natural-language description
base_model: Deepseek-R1 for input-file generation and Deepseek-V3 for other modules
tools_used: the MOOSE framework executables running the generated input decks, with FAISS and BGE-M3 retrieval over MOOSE documentation and more than 8,000 annotated example input files
evaluation_method: nine test cases spanning heat conduction, elasticity, plasticity, porous media, phase change, phase field, fuel assembly and thermal-mechanical coupling, each repeated five times, scored by success rate and token cost with a retrieval ablation
baseline: none externally; an ablation with and without the retrieval knowledge base
reported_result: an average success rate of 93% at an average cost of less than 1 yuan per case, with plasticity the worst case at 60%
maturity_claimed: MooseAgent can largely automate the simulation process
author_stated_limitations: the authors report poor performance on plasticity at 60% success, that the LLM struggles selecting correct functions from the vast library, a lack of accuracy in MOOSE fundamentals such as function expressions and input card format, and the infinite-loop failure mode

title: A fine-tuned large language model based molecular dynamics agent for code generation to obtain material thermodynamic parameters
authors: Zhuofan Shi; Chunxiao Xin; Tong Huo; Yuntao Jiang; Bowen Wu; Xingyue Chen; Wei Qin; Xinjian Ma; Gang Huang; Zhenyu Wang; Jing Xiang
task: generating, executing and refining LAMMPS molecular-dynamics code to obtain material thermodynamic parameters from natural-language requests
base_model: not stated - a fine-tuned LAMMPSLLM built with QLoRA, but the parent model is never named
tools_used: LAMMPS, a Docker container for code execution, a curated LAMMPS script corpus and a user-facing interface
evaluation_method: an expert user study in which participants specified molecular dynamics tasks in natural language, interactions were monitored and experts rated every task, plus comparison of the fine-tuned model against non-fine-tuned models of similar size
baseline: large models of similar size that had not been fine-tuned
reported_result: reduces the average task time by 42.22% compared to traditional models
maturity_claimed: MDAgent can effectively assist experts in semi-automating domain-specific tasks, serving as a valuable support tool.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state MDAgent is currently a semi-automated intelligent assistant because current local small-parameter LLMs are not yet sufficient to automatically run all complex codes

title: FEABench: Evaluating Language Models on Multiphysics Reasoning Ability
authors: Nayantara Mudur; Hao Cui; Subhashini Venugopalan; Paul Raccuglia; Michael P. Brenner; Peter Nørgaard
task: a benchmark plus a reference multi-agent baseline for LLMs that operate finite element analysis software through its API
base_model: Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Gemma-2-27B-IT, Gemma-2-9B-IT and CodeGemma-7B-IT
tools_used: COMSOL Multiphysics via its Java API driven from Python through JPype and MPh, an annotated code-snippet retrieval tool and a model-tree comparison evaluator
evaluation_method: FEABench Gold of 15 manually verified problems and FEABench Large of 200 algorithmically parsed problems from the COMSOL Application Gallery, scored on executability, whether a target value is exported, relative error and model-tree similarity
baseline: single-turn one-shot prompting of each model, plus ground-truth COMSOL code and target values
reported_result: the best performing strategy generates executable API calls 88% of the time; only 2 of 15 FEABench Gold problems had a valid target computed in multi-turn agent mode
maturity_claimed: LLMs that can successfully interact with and operate FEA software to solve problems such as those in our benchmark would push the frontiers of automation in engineering.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the benchmark is restricted to simpler geometries without CAD imports and to problems solving in under a minute, that the physics block is the hardest component, and that adding more human-verified problems would be valuable

title: TritonDFT: Automating DFT with a Multi-Agent Framework
authors: Zhengding Hu; Kuntal Talit; Zhen Wang; Haseeb Ahmad; Yichen Lin; Prabhleen Kaur; Christopher Lane; Elizabeth A. Peterson; Zhiting Hu; Elizabeth Nowadnick; Yufei Ding
task: end-to-end automation of DFT calculations in Quantum ESPRESSO including Pareto-optimal selection of accuracy-versus-cost parameters
base_model: eight models benchmarked - GPT 5.2, GPT 5.1, GPT 4o, GPT 4o mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5
tools_used: Quantum ESPRESSO v7.4 executables pw.x, ph.x, q2r.x and matdyn.x, with MPI/OpenMP launch and Slurm submission and a web user interface
evaluation_method: DFTBench, comprising 73 unique crystalline materials with expert-curated convergence references costing over 500 CPU-hours, with pass rates per model across ten material categories and three energy-deviation targets
baseline: manual PhD-level expert execution at under one request per hour
reported_result: more than 10 times acceleration over manual expert execution, at a per-query LLM cost of roughly $0.01 to $0.44, with under 6% pass rate on magnetic materials
maturity_claimed: TritonDFT provides an open user interface for real-world usage
author_stated_limitations: the authors state performance degrades on more complex systems, particularly magnetic materials where all models exhibit pass rates below 6%, that the system is limited to Quantum ESPRESSO, and that band-gap extraction is problematic in smeared calculations

title: Toward Greater Autonomy in Materials Discovery Agents: Unifying Planning, Physics, and Scientists
authors: Zhou, Lianhao; Hongyi Ling; Keqiang Yan; Kaiji Zhao; Xiaoning Qian; Raymundo Arróyave; Xiaofeng Qian; Shuiwang Ji
task: plan and execute crystal-structure generation, structure prediction and property-targeted materials discovery from high-level goals
base_model: OpenAI models via the API; the backbone for the main result tables is not explicitly named
tools_used: CHGNet and M3GNet machine-learned force fields, ASE relaxation, pymatgen structure matching and space-group analysis, SMACT validity checks and retrieval over MP-20, Matbench and JARVIS-DFT
evaluation_method: benchmark comparison against generative-model baselines on MP-20, Matbench, MPTS-52 and a challenge set, scored on validity, metastability, DFT stability, stable-unique-novel rate, match rate and RMSE, plus a workflow-validity study across three LLMs with and without human intuition
baseline: CDVAE, DiffCSP, FlowMM, CrystalTextLLM, FlowLLM, MatLLMSearch, CrystaLLM and Mat2Seq
