maturity_claimed: MAPPS is a promising framework for autonomous materials discovery
author_stated_limitations: the authors state MAPPS currently has a human expert in the loop and does not reach the fully autonomous Level 3, that it focuses on materials discovery with extensions to molecules and polymers underexplored, and that many LLMs consistently produce five-step workflows often including useless or redundant steps

title: LQCDMaster: Agentic Scientific Computing for Lattice Quantum Chromodynamics Research
authors: He Gao; Tingjia Miao; Wenkai Jin; Muhua Zhang; Hanzhang Wang; Jie Ran; Jinxin Tan; Zhentao Zhang; B Tang; Leiyi Li; Jun 俊 Hua 华; X. Jiang
task: convert natural-language lattice-QCD research requests into executable PyQUDA measurement workflows and job submissions
base_model: GPT-5.4 for the main results, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro used for a full cross-backbone repeat
tools_used: PyQUDA on QUDA/GPU, SLURM job submission, a deterministic Wick-contraction engine, static analysis, test execution and LLM critique
evaluation_method: a 70-task benchmark across five observable classes on one named ensemble, with every generated workflow executed and numerically compared against a hand-written expert reference implementation at machine precision
baseline: hand-written expert reference implementations, Claude Code as a general coding agent, and a DeepSeek-V4-Pro backbone variant
reported_result: 63 of 70 workflows reproduce expert implementations at machine precision, 90.0% accuracy, with speedups of 17 to 54 times; Claude Code failed to yield executable scripts for any of the 20 local two-point-function tasks
maturity_claimed: This work pioneers the paradigm of agentic scientific computing by automating the end-to-end scientific computing workflows in lattice QCD research
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the benchmark covers representative but not exhaustive tasks, that executable code and static consistency checks are insufficient for validating baryon contraction logic so direct numerical regression against trusted references remains necessary, and that for new observable classes reference comparisons and human review remain essential

title: MADE: Benchmark Environments for Closed-Loop Materials Discovery
authors: Shreshth A. Malik; Tiarnan A. S. Doherty; Panagiotis Tigas; Muhammed Razzak; Stephen J. Roberts; A. T. Walsh; Yarin Gal
task: benchmark closed-loop materials-discovery policies that propose, evaluate and refine candidate crystal structures under a fixed oracle budget
tools_used: the Chemeleon crystal generator, a random structure generator, a MACE machine-learned-potential scorer, an orb-v3 energy oracle, pymatgen convex-hull machinery and the Materials Project API
evaluation_method: 5 independent episodes per chemical system with 50 oracle queries each, averaged over 10 systems for ternary, quaternary and quinary intermetallic spaces, scored on stable-unique-novel rate, area under the discovery curve and acceleration and enhancement factors
baseline: a random generator with random planner and random selector, plus diversity-planner, LLM-planner, Chemeleon and Chemeleon-plus-MLIP modular pipelines
reported_result: the fully agentic orchestrator achieves an enhancement factor of 6.0, against a best non-agentic pipeline acceleration factor of 6.4
maturity_claimed: MADE provides a concrete testbed for evaluating core capabilities of agentic systems in realistic scientific discovery settings, including long-horizon planning, reasoning under uncertainty, and learning from feedback.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state current experiments rely on generators and machine-learned potentials trained on Materials Project data and thus inherit shared distributional biases that may simplify discovery relative to real-world settings, and that extending to DFT or experimental oracles and multi-objective tasks are natural next steps

title: R-LAM: Reproducibility-Constrained Large Action Models for Scientific Workflow Automation
authors: Suriya Sureshkumar
task: enforce deterministic, auditable, replayable execution when an LLM planner drives a scientific workflow
base_model: not stated - LLM interaction is performed via API with temperature 0.0 but no model name is given
tools_used: Python action adapters wrapping scikit-learn data loading, statistical analysis, feature standardisation, logistic-regression training and evaluation, with a CLI, a programmatic API and a trace store
evaluation_method: three falsifiable evaluation questions - replay correctness, fork isolation and failure auditability - run on minimal synthetic workflows plus one scikit-learn workflow, compared across three pipelines over 5 to 10 repeats
baseline: a deterministic script-based pipeline with no LAM involvement and a naive LAM-driven pipeline with no reproducibility constraints
reported_result: all three pipelines achieved identical final accuracy of 0.9877; R-LAM scored 1.0 on replay, trace and failure with variance 0.0, against 0.0, 0.0 and 1.0 with variance 1.0 for the naive LAM
maturity_claimed: This work does not claim autonomous scientific discovery or fully automated research. The framework is designed to assist, not replace, human scientific judgment.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the evaluation is at small to moderate scale on representative workflows rather than large long-running pipelines, that it does not involve real laboratory hardware or cyber-physical systems, that the framework inherits the probabilistic limitations of its planning LLM, and that it assumes external tools behave deterministically

title: Reasoning-agent-driven process simulation, optimization, carbon accounting and decarbonization of distillation
authors: Shudan Tan; X. Zhou; Hai Zhou; Zhimian Hao; Yihang Xie; Liwei Cao; Guofei Shen; Yunhu Gao; Qun Shen; Wei Wei
task: automate Aspen Plus distillation simulation, optimisation, heat-pump retrofit design and greenhouse-gas accounting from natural-language prompts
tools_used: Aspen Plus via generated input files and API import and export, MCP tools for GitHub, file system, web search and crawling, LangChain tool calling, and a retrieval system over 100+ documents for emission factors
evaluation_method: a single proof-of-concept case study separating a 100 kg per hour methanol-ethanol feed to 98 wt% purity, with shortcut then rigorous column simulation, sensitivity analysis, design specification, a heat-pump variant and emission accounting under three energy scenarios, all manually verified by the authors
baseline: none - the comparison is between three energy-supply scenarios and between the traditional and heat-pump-assisted process
reported_result: the coal-based scenario had the highest emissions at 20.3 kg CO2e per hour, dropping 44% and 93% in the natural gas and renewable scenarios; the heat pump saved 53.7 kW of steam for 10.7 kW of electricity, an 80% energy saving, and the combination cut carbon emission by 98%
maturity_claimed: The developed agent served as a prototype that successfully integrated reasoning with the Reasoning-Acting framework, with its current efficacy being shaped by both prompts and selection of LLMs.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the workflow was pre-defined in the prompts for this case study, that tackling problems exceeding token limits would require autonomous agentic task decomposition, that each run took around 4 hours, and that embodied equipment emissions are assumed negligible

title: Empowering Automated Process Analysis through LLM-Based Literature Mining, Flowsheet Digitization, and Simulation
authors: Jan-Frederic Laub
task: mine literature for chemical process knowledge, digitise flowsheets from natural-language descriptions and translate them into runnable process simulations for sustainability assessment
tools_used: an established commercial process simulator, unnamed, plus rigorous thermodynamic calculations, black-box optimisation routines and a literature-derived knowledge base
evaluation_method: comparison of the collected and digitised process information against expert-curated datasets and manually drawn flowsheets, and of the generated simulations against expert interpretations
baseline: expert-curated datasets, manually drawn flowsheets and expert interpretations of the same processes
reported_result: the generated process simulations are on par with expert interpretations with significantly less manual effort; no number, unit or count is given anywhere in the abstract
maturity_claimed: We show that our integrated pipelines can faithfully collect and digitize chemical process information
author_stated_limitations: none stated - the record is a two-page extended abstract with no limitations or future-work text; the only qualifier offered is that potential simplifications necessary to achieve convergence are recorded transparently

title: Retrieval-Augmented Instruction Tuning for Automated Process Engineering Calculations : A Tool-Chaining Problem-Solving Framework with Attributable Reflection
authors: Sagar Srinivas Sakhinana; Geethan Sannidhi; Venkataramana Runkana
task: generate, execute, debug and refine Python programs that chain numerical tools to solve chemical and process engineering calculations
base_model: instruction-tuned CodeGemma-7b-it and CodeLlama-7b-hf with 4-bit QLoRA
tools_used: SciPy including solve_ivp, NumPy, Matplotlib, the Wolfram Alpha and Stack Overflow APIs, code documentation, a code interpreter and a program cache
evaluation_method: a 70/15/15 split of two custom-curated datasets with a four-stage metric suite covering task planning, tool selection, tool calling and response generation, plus five ablations
baseline: GPT-4 Omni, GPT-4 Turbo-preview, Claude-3 Opus and Gemini Pro, plus ablated variants of the framework
reported_result: tool usage awareness 86.89%, pass rate 82.34% and accuracy 84.21% against GPT-4 Omni at 95.12, 90.45 and 92.78
maturity_claimed: our framework matches the performance of large-scale proprietary models on benchmark datasets, proving its effectiveness and usability
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the proposed framework is effective but lags slightly behind the proprietary models, and name more diverse instruction-tuning datasets, a wider range of external tools and improved explainability as future work

title: OpenFOAMGPT 2.0: End-to-end, trustworthy automation for computational fluid dynamics
authors: Jingsen Feng; Ran Xu; Xu Chu
venue: International Journal of Heat and Fluid Flow
task: turn a natural-language query into a complete OpenFOAM CFD study - meshing, case setup, execution, parametric sweep and post-processing
tools_used: OpenFOAM v2406 in a Docker container with blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, icoFoam and multiphase solvers, the Allrun script and log capture, plus ParaView output and generated Python plotting
evaluation_method: five case studies with repeated execution - single-phase Poiseuille flow against the analytical solution, multi-phase Poiseuille flow, single-phase and multi-phase porous media flow and motorbike aerodynamics over ten velocities - with a trustworthiness table of repeat counts and two extended runs of 100 continuous simulations
baseline: none quantitative; the single-phase Poiseuille case is checked against an analytical solution
reported_result: 100% success and reproducibility rates across over 450 simulations, with permeability at the finest mesh differing by less than 2% from the coarser mesh
maturity_claimed: Rigorous trustworthiness verification confirms that properly designed multi-agent systems can achieve the reliability standards necessary for zero-tolerance scientific computing applications while significantly lowering entry barriers.
author_stated_limitations: the authors concede very little - the only qualifiers are conditional, that the 100% success rate holds when provided with well-formulated user queries under carefully designed system prompts, and that LLM-generated configuration files may occasionally contain errors; no dedicated limitations section exists

title: Early Experiences Using AI Software Agents on OLCF Systems: From Installation and Environments to Simulation Workflows for Molecular and Materials Sciences
authors: Ada Sedova; Mathieu Taillefumier; Óscar Hernández
task: use off-the-shelf AI coding agents to build, deploy, test and prototype molecular-simulation and machine-learned-interatomic-potential workflows on leadership-class HPC
base_model: Codex with GPT 5.4 in high accuracy mode, and Claude Code v2.1.232
tools_used: Frontier and Wombat login and batch shells with modules, Slurm, srun and torchrun; Spack v1.2.2; a CP2K build; MACE 0.3.15 with MACE-OFF23; the ACEsuit LAMMPS fork with ML-MACE and Kokkos/HIP; OpenMM with AMOEBA; ASE; PyTorch 2.8.0 with ROCm 6.4
evaluation_method: early-experience case studies across three research questions - build and deploy, scientific method development, theory development - on named OLCF systems, with no controlled benchmark and no baseline arm
baseline: an unassisted expert human, estimated informally rather than measured
reported_result: the overall speedup for difficult technical tasks "can approach several orders of magnitude", the theory-to-test loop estimated at over 1,000 times, Spack environment generation in 10 to 20 minutes against one to two hours, and a distributed-launch sweep in which torchrun passed all seven tested cases while Slurm and MPI launches failed all seven
maturity_claimed: Under expert supervision and with file-based provenance, AI coding systems could reduce the translation cost between scientific intent and machine-specific execution
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that the amount of work that must be verified grows with AI reliability, faithfulness and reproducibility problems and "in the case of HPC production workflows, can become unmanageable", that the file volume from even a short agent session "can rapidly become overwhelming for human verification", that language models produce coherent plausible explanations which "can lead to over confidence in their methods, summaries and outputs", that the results are platform-specific, and that faithful evidence and provenance requirements "are currently out of the scope of state-of-the-art tools"

title: Fine-tuning a large language model for automating computational fluid dynamics simulations
authors: Zhehao Dong; Zhen Lu; Yang Yue
task: translate a natural-language CFD problem description plus mesh files into an executable OpenFOAM case and run it to convergence
base_model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fine-tuned with LoRA as the generator and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for the pre-checker, runner and corrector agents, orchestrated with MetaGPT v0.8.1
tools_used: OpenFOAM-v2406 with icoFoam, simpleFoam, pisoFoam and pimpleFoam, mesh files, generated execution scripts and real-time log monitoring
evaluation_method: a 21-case incompressible benchmark of 10 laminar and 11 turbulent flows with Reynolds numbers from 40 to one million, ten independent experiments per case, scored on accuracy against benchmark solutions, first-attempt pass rate, correction iterations, token usage and cost, plus a chain-of-thought ablation
baseline: MetaOpenFOAM driven by GPT-4o, and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1 and Llama3.3-70B-Instruct substituted into the same multi-agent framework
reported_result: 88.7% solution accuracy and 82.6% first-attempt success rate, with 2.6 correction iterations against 7.2 for the runner-up, at 0.020 US dollars per solution; without chain-of-thought annotations accuracy fell to 78.2% and pass@1 to 61.7%
maturity_claimed: Evaluation on a benchmark of 21 diverse flow cases demonstrates state-of-the-art performance
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that while the method performs well for incompressible benchmarks, limitations remain for more complex simulations, and name multiphase flows, compressible flows and heat transfer as future work; failure analysis found most errors in turbulence simulations, caused by divergence from unreasonable parameter values such as dissipation rates set orders of magnitude too high

title: Large language model-assisted sensitivity analysis and parameter optimization in computational fluid dynamics
authors: Chen Yuxuan; Long Zhang; Zhu Xu; Zhou Hua; Ren Zhuyin
task: perform CFD sensitivity analysis and parameter optimisation from natural-language input by sampling, running many OpenFOAM simulations through MetaOpenFOAM 2.0 and invoking external analysis and optimisation libraries
base_model: GPT-4o at temperature 0.01, with OpenAIEmbeddings for the retrieval vector store
tools_used: MetaOpenFOAM 2.0, OpenFOAM 10 including reactingFoam, the L-BFGS-B routine from scipy.optimize, an active-subspace sensitivity library with OLS and QPHD regression, LangChain v0.1.19 with a FAISS vector store and MetaGPT v0.8.0
evaluation_method: 11 distinct CFD tasks over five case studies - PitzDaily, CounterFlowFlame2D, BuoyantCavity, homogeneous isotropic turbulence, and a hydrogen combustion chamber that the authors describe as "a non-OpenFOAM tutorial" external validation case - plus a prompt-robustness study comparing pass@1 on an original prompt dataset against a semantically equivalent but syntactically different one
baseline: none for the CFD tasks; the authors state executability, pass@k and iteration counts remain those previously reported for MetaOpenFOAM 2.0. The robustness study compares two prompt datasets against each other
reported_result: 11 CFD tasks driven from concise natural-language commands of roughly 200 characters, "translating into over 2,000 lines of automated code execution", with a final optimised equivalence ratio of 1.09; pass@1 of 86.6% on the original prompt dataset against 85.0% on a paraphrased one
maturity_claimed: These findings underline the transformative potential of LLM-driven frameworks in revolutionizing CFD simulation workflows, making them more accessible, efficient, and effective for both industrial and research applications.
author_stated_limitations: there is no limitations section. The only limitation stated in the authors' own terms is that the propagation distance is confined between 0 and 0.0707 by the physics of the case, so "owing to these inherent bounds, the fitted response surface is not perfect". The published version adds a bounded robustness claim rather than a limitation: "OptMetaOpenFOAM maintains nearly identical success rates when handling semantically equivalent but syntactically different inputs"

title: OASiS: an open-source multi-physics and multi-code framework for verified computer simulations
authors: Alexander Hermann; Arman Shojaei; Ingo Scheider; Christian Cyron
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
task: expose eight independently developed finite-element codes to a general-purpose LLM coding agent over the Model Context Protocol so the agent can set up, run, couple, extend and verify simulations
base_model: not stated - the server is model-agnostic; Claude Code is recommended for sub-agent spawning, with Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex also configured, and the stress tests were run in a fresh interactive Claude terminal
tools_used: 13 MCP tools over FEniCSx, deal.II, 4C Multiphysics, NGSolve, scikit-fem, Kratos Multiphysics, DUNE-fem and FEBio, plus Gmsh mesh generation, preCICE and domain-decomposition coupling across seven coupling modes and twenty solver pairs, solver source browsing and rebuilding, and ParaView or PyVista visualisation
evaluation_method: 24 end-to-end stress tests, each a single verbatim natural-language prompt given to a fresh agent with no additional guidance, scored pass or fail against analytical solutions, literature values or cross-solver agreement, plus over 400 unit tests
baseline: none; cross-solver agreement and analytical or literature reference values serve as the check
reported_result: 24 of 24 stress tests pass, with seven solvers agreeing to 99.9% on the cross-solver Poisson benchmark, an L2 error of 7e-15 on the heat-equation test, 0.42% L2 error against the Lame solution, and settlement and pressure errors of 0.1% and under 0.4% on the 4C Terzaghi case
maturity_claimed: A general-purpose, solver-agnostic MCP server that makes an AI agent as knowledgeable as an expert user of EVERY supported FEM code. Not a wrapper. Not a tutorial replayer.
author_stated_limitations: the repository documents failures per test rather than a limitations section: deal.II test 3 needed five iterations for correct C++ and hit six API and mesh incompatibilities, the 4C test first produced a silently failing variable resolution with velocities thirty times too low and an MPI_ABORT that swallowed error messages, FEBio is listed as unavailable because it needs a binary, and contributors are warned off benchmark-specific parameter databases and model-specific templates as fine-tuning

title: M.A.R.V.I.N. – A Software-Led Infrastructure for Thermodynamically Grounded Autonomous Materials Discovery
authors: Michael Bustamante; Bustamante Gabriel
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
task: anchor an autonomous materials-discovery loop to CALPHAD-assessed Gibbs energy functions, demonstrated on garnet-type lithium lanthanum zirconate
base_model: not stated - no LLM, model family or version is named anywhere in the paper
tools_used: designed MCP tool contracts over pycalphad for equilibrium, ESPEI for Bayesian MCMC database assessment and kawin for precipitation kinetics, plus the authors own self-contained SGTE Gibbs evaluator, a compound-energy-formalism solver, a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC sampler and a SQLite and NetworkX knowledge graph
evaluation_method: a single computational case study comparing computed atmosphere diagrams, sublattice vacancy partitioning and Nernst-Einstein conductivity against published experimental and tabulated data; no agent, loop or autonomy is evaluated
baseline: published literature data including Allen et al. 2012 conductivity, Rettenwander et al. 2016 neutron-diffraction site occupancies, NIST-JANAF and Knacke tabulations, Dinsdale SGTE91 unaries and the Chang and Hallstedt Li-O database
reported_result: ionic conductivity estimates matching the experimental 0.87 millisiemens per centimetre at a tantalum fraction of 0.125 by diffusivity calibration, a lithium carbonate formation boundary at log carbon-dioxide pressure of -5.6 plus or minus 0.6 dex, SGTE unaries anchored to within 0.001 joules per mole, and eight MCMC chains reaching Gelman-Rubin below 1.05
maturity_claimed: M.A.R.V.I.N. provides generalizable, software-led architecture for reproducible materials discovery.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that the ESPEI assessment is ongoing, that the conductivity estimate "is a calibrated consistency check rather than a blind prediction", that the atmosphere diagram is a ternary proxy rather than a full multicomponent garnet calculation, that the Nernst-Einstein model is a dilute-solution approximation applied outside its strict domain of validity to a system with around 40% octahedral vacancies, that the kawin precipitation module "cannot be exercised for LLZO", and that equilibrium phase stability is "a necessary but not sufficient condition for synthesis prediction"
code_availability: Zenodo deposit doi:10.5281/zenodo.19835550 under CC-BY 4.0, shipping the thermodynamic database, ESPEI input and datasets, the MCMC trace and four Python modules

title: CFDLLMBench: A Benchmark Suite for Evaluating Large Language Models in Computational Fluid Dynamics
authors: Nithin Somasekharan; Ling Yue; Yadi Cao; Weichao Li; Patrick Emami; Pochinapeddi Sai Bhargav; Anurag Acharya; Xingyu Xie; Shaowu Pan
task: benchmark language models and agent frameworks on graduate-level CFD knowledge, PDE solver coding, and end-to-end OpenFOAM case setup and execution
base_model: Claude Sonnet 3.5, o3-mini, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Haiku 3.5 and Gemma-2-9B-IT, with decoding temperature set to zero where configurable
tools_used: OpenFOAM v10 utilities and input files, Python numerical libraries for PDE solvers, a retrieval store of similar simulation files and Docker containerisation
evaluation_method: three datasets - 90 multiple-choice questions, 24 PDE programming tasks, and 126 OpenFOAM cases comprising 110 basic and 16 advanced - scored by a success rate aggregating executability, relative numerical error, numerical convergence and, for the OpenFOAM set, folder and file structure, file similarity, normalised mean squared error and physical accuracy
baseline: zero-shot prompting as the no-agent baseline, and MetaOpenFOAM against Foam-Agent as competing harnesses
reported_result: the best model reaches 92% on the knowledge questions but only 14% on the coding benchmark and 34% on basic and 25% on advanced OpenFOAM cases; zero-shot prompting is close to 0%, and removing either retrieval or the reviewer agent costs roughly 10 percentage points
maturity_claimed: CFDLLMBench establishes a solid foundation for the development and evaluation of LLM-driven automation of numerical experiments for complex physical systems.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that establishing appropriate human references "is non-trivial because performance depends strongly on the evaluator's domain knowledge and experience", that formal human baselines remain future work, that "the lack of spatial reasoning capabilities in LLMs appears to produce an incorrect geometry and mesh" and that geometry understanding "is a major area in need of improvement", and that models "often fail to fully understand the prompts and lack domain-specific reasoning"

title: ChatCFD: A Large Language Model‐Driven Agent for End‐to‐End Computational Fluid Dynamics Automation with Structured Knowledge and Reasoning
authors: Enguo Fan; Kang Hu; Zhuowen Wu; Jie Ge; Jiawei Miao; Yu Zhang; He Sun; Weizong Wang; Tianhan Zhang
task: configure and execute OpenFOAM simulations end-to-end from a natural-language description, an uploaded research article or a mesh file
base_model: DeepSeek-R1 for reasoning, parameter extraction, error analysis and reflection, and DeepSeek-V3 for structured low-complexity tasks, file validation and suspicious-file detection
tools_used: OpenFOAM solvers including simpleFoam, rhoCentralFoam and pisoFoam, fluentMeshToFoam mesh conversion, a structured JSON knowledge base and a vector database built from OpenFOAM manuals and tutorials, two retrieval modules, sentence-transformers embeddings, pydantic structured outputs and a Streamlit interface
evaluation_method: 205 OpenFOAM tutorial and wiki benchmark cases plus 110 perturbed variants and two literature-derived cases, scored on execution success rate, a three-tier physical-fidelity protocol, token and cost accounting, a six-arm ablation and flexibility experiments on solver and turbulence-model switching
baseline: MetaOpenFOAM and Foam-Agent
reported_result: 82.1% execution success against 6.2% for MetaOpenFOAM and 42.3% for Foam-Agent, with 68.12% physical fidelity and 97.4% summary fidelity at 192,100 tokens and 0.208 US dollars per case; solver selection succeeded in 95.23% of cases and turbulence-model switching in 100%
maturity_claimed: ChatCFD establishes new benchmarks for AI-driven CFD automation
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that language models "excel at high-level linguistic narration but consistently struggle to enforce the complete chain of physical constraints within the generated executable code", that "reflections beyond 75% of the limit (approximately 22 iterations) often fail to resolve remaining errors", that all agents show lower success rates in combustion and multiphase flow, that DeepSeek-R1 hallucinations such as spurious Markdown formatting persist despite prompt engineering and structured outputs, and that mesh support is limited to Fluent meshes and existing polyMesh directories

title: An Agentic Orchestration of Atomistic Simulations
authors: Rahul Somasundaram; Adela Habib; Khanh Dang; Sachin Shivakumar; Ryley G. Hill; Golo Wimmer; Avanish Mishra; Aleksandra Pachalieva; Arthur Lui; Hari Viswanathan; Michael Grosskopf; Saryu Fensin
task: run an end-to-end molecular-dynamics workflow - interatomic-potential selection and download, LAMMPS input-script authoring, execution, error recovery and post-processing - from a natural-language prompt
base_model: GPT-5.2 for potential selection and GPT-5 as the backend for the benchmarks
tools_used: LAMMPS executed via MPI or Kokkos on GPUs, the atomman package to enumerate potentials, the NIST interatomic potentials repository, the URSA execution agent write-code tool for Python post-processing, the URSA arXiv agent with the arXiv search API, and LangGraph
evaluation_method: head-to-head benchmarking against LAVA, a Python toolkit for LAMMPS and VASP property calculations, on aluminium properties - cohesive energy, lattice constant, cold curve, thermal expansion, liquid radial distribution function, melting temperature, generalized stacking fault energy, elastic properties, Bain paths and defect formation energies - under three prompting regimes, plus a side-by-side comparison of generated input decks against another agentic framework
baseline: the LAVA toolkit, published melting-temperature values, and the multi-agentic framework of Vriza et al. for potential selection and melting-temperature decks
reported_result: cohesive energy and lattice constant in complete agreement with LAVA, excellent agreement on the cold curve and thermal expansion, a melting temperature consistent with LAVA once a detailed coexistence-and-bisection prompt was supplied, and a generated simulation cell roughly a third the linear size of the comparison framework at four times the steps per iteration
maturity_claimed: our work significantly accelerates the adoption of agentic AI enabled workflows for the design and discovery of novel materials
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that the agent could not reproduce the generalized stacking fault energy calculation from a minimal prompt, that the thermal-expansion run covered only part of the temperature range because the range was not specified in the prompt, that a melting-temperature discrepancy was attributable to "the lack of the LLM's knowledge about the two-phase method", and that protocols "can vary substantially across agentic frameworks, even when pursuing the same scientific objective", underscoring the need for benchmarks evaluating both predictions and workflows

title: NeuroClaw Technical Report
authors: Cheng Wang; Zhibin He; Zhihao Peng; Shengyuan Liu; Yufan Hu; Carl Yang; Lifang He; Lichao Sun; Xiang Li; Yixuan Yuan
task: run multi-stage neuroimaging preprocessing and analysis pipelines end-to-end from raw data and a written task specification
base_model: ten evaluated backends - Claude-Opus-4.6, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, DeepSeek-3.2, Gemini-3-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Pro, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, Grok-4.2, MiniMax-M2.7 and Qwen3-plus - with GPT-5.4 as the fixed judge
tools_used: FSL, FreeSurfer, fMRIPrep, QSIPrep and ANTs, plus DICOM-to-NIfTI conversion, BIDS validation, single-command execution, and management of Python environments, Docker containers and GPU stacks
evaluation_method: NeuroBench, 100 hand-written task specifications across structural MRI, functional MRI, diffusion MRI and EEG on ADNI and HCP Young Adult data, run with and without the skill library for each backend, roughly five repetitions each, scored one to ten on planning completeness, tool and skill usage reasonableness and command correctness by a fixed judge model
baseline: the same base model invoked without the NeuroClaw skill library
reported_result: all ten base models improve inside the framework, with an average absolute gain of 4.74 points, a top score of 72.10% for Claude-Opus-4.6 against 69.12% without skills, and a largest gain of 12.97 points for MiniMax-M2.7
maturity_claimed: strong benchmark performance should be interpreted as infrastructure readiness rather than clinical readiness
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the work "does not claim state-of-the-art performance or present exhaustive cross-system leaderboards", that they "do not evaluate model quality for clinical outcomes or make regulatory claims", that the tasks "represent only a subset of real-world neuroimaging complexity", that the protocol "may underestimate the effect of skill usage in real deployments", and that cautious reasoning "can be partially penalized by the judge as extraneous to the narrow task requirement", so the gains "should therefore be interpreted conservatively"

title: Autonomous heterogeneous catalyst discovery with a self-evolving multi-agent digital twin
authors: Zhilong Song; Zongmin Zhang; Lixue Cheng
task: autonomously build a condition-aware atomistic-to-kinetic model of a working catalyst and search for new catalyst candidates
base_model: DeepSeek V4 Pro for four agents, GPT-5.5 for three, and Codex with a GPT-5.5 backend for the coordinator; the authors state the system is foundation-model-agnostic
tools_used: 27 scientific tools including SurFF surface free-energy prediction, VSSR-MC surface reconstruction, AdsorbDiff adsorption-site sampling, the UMA universal machine-learned potential, two-phase climbing-image nudged elastic band, slow-growth molecular dynamics, the CatMAP microkinetic solver, electrochemical kinetic Monte Carlo, an RDKit bond-operation enumerator and a 569-species thermochemistry database
evaluation_method: seven gas-solid thermal-catalysis benchmarks compared against published experiment and DFT, a 60-episode reinforcement-learning training run on 600 surfaces with a fixed 50-case holdout, a twelve-prompt five-run skill ablation against a bare frontier coding agent, and a five-round closed-loop propane-dehydrogenation discovery campaign
baseline: the CARE exhaustive reaction-network generator, a frontier coding agent without the CatDT skill, a stateless agent and eight memory and reinforcement-learning ablation configurations, and published DFT and experimental references
reported_result: every prediction lies between 0.5 and 2 times the corresponding experimental value across measurements spanning four orders of magnitude, the held-out pass rate climbs from 41.2% to 83.5%, the mechanism enumerator needs 97 potential evaluations in 635 seconds against 39,893 intermediates for the exhaustive baseline, and the discovery loop proposes a candidate with a predicted turnover frequency of 1.63 per second at nearly 100% selectivity
maturity_claimed: CatDT demonstrates that the full theoretical catalysis pipeline, from a bulk crystal to experimentally comparable kinetic observables, can be made autonomous, self-improving, and quantitatively predictive.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that predicted propylene selectivity "underestimates experiment because the multi-path KMC is not yet coupled to UniMech's Sabatier gating, an integration left to follow-on work", that residual barrier offsets are "a residual attributable to the UMA-DFT methodological difference", that a kinetic dissection and synthesis-feasibility assessment of the leading candidates "lies outside the scope of the present infrastructure paper", and that machine-learned-potential backends still require separate training per target system
code_availability: the package is stated as forthcoming at https://github.com/AI4QC/catdt upon publication, not yet released

title: A Preliminary Assessment of Coding Agents for CFD Workflows
authors: Ke Xiao; Haoze Zhang; Yangchen Xu; Runze Mao; Han Li; Zhi X. Chen
task: set up, mesh, run and repair OpenFOAM cases end-to-end from a natural-language task description
base_model: MiniMax-M2.1 for the tutorial-derivative tasks and GPT-5.2 for the obstacle-flow tasks, both inside the OpenCode agent loop
tools_used: bash, read and edit function calls; OpenFOAM utilities including blockMesh, snappyHexMesh, rhoCentralFoam and pimpleFoam; Gmsh including its Python API; Python; and shell search tools over the local tutorial tree
evaluation_method: a single-run protocol on FoamBench-Advanced, evaluating nine tutorial-derivative cases and four planar obstacle-flow cases on completion to end time, structure and content similarity and field normalised mean squared error, with token and tool-call counts logged
baseline: the default OpenCode build-agent system prompt as a prompt ablation, and a MiniMax-M2.1 against GPT-5.2 backbone comparison
reported_result: the CFD-focused prompt completes all nine runs against four of nine under the default prompt, with mean similarity scores of 0.986 and 0.919 and seven of nine cases meeting the error threshold
maturity_claimed: Overall, we conclude that LLM agents show promise for CFD workflows, particularly for simpler tasks like 2D simulations.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that errors requiring "a deeper understanding of the underlying physics, which the agent currently lacks" are more challenging, so "human oversight remains essential", that "agent performance degrades as geometric complexity and physical stiffness increase", that extending to complex three-dimensional or industrial workflows "will require careful investigation and development", and that mesh quality is "largely determined by the LLM model itself"

title: Corridor: an AI-orchestrated repair-and-scoring pipeline for finite-element validation models
authors: Chintan Shelat
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
task: diagnose, repair and score finite-element validation decks against published experimental corridors
base_model: a Sonnet-class model from Anthropic; the exact version is not stated
tools_used: deck inspection and block match-and-replace editing of LS-DYNA-format keyword files, the OpenRadioss solver including disposable scratch-probe re-runs, energy-balance and mass-error log parsing, an objective-rating-metrics library for ISO/TS 18571 scoring and a pre-flight triage command
evaluation_method: live runs of the repair agent on four real, structurally distinct decks with real logged solver output and logged API cost, the sweep and analyst agents demonstrated on a fifth structurally unrelated deck, and three adversarial attempts to induce a static-context fix proposal
baseline: an independently produced manual repair of the same defect
reported_result: a fully automated investigate, propose, approve, apply and verify cycle on four of four real models, five of five sweep points reaching clean solver termination, three of three adversarial attempts declined, and roughly 0.39 US dollars of total logged model spend
maturity_claimed: The Repair Agent reached a fully automated investigate to propose to approve to apply to verify cycle on all four, correctly distinguishing genuine defects from superficially identical ones across structurally different decks.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the defect taxonomy "is seeded from defects actually encountered during development, not a comprehensive catalog", that every reported score "is a single-channel measurement; it is not a whole-model validation claim", that the verification gate "checks aggregate energy-balance and mass-added figures at the final solved cycle rather than the full time history", so "a transient event that self-resolves by the final cycle would pass the gate" and "hourglass energy is not currently checked", that API spend "is gated per call rather than per session", that escalation messages go to stdout rather than a machine-readable channel, and that the analyst agent "does not perform further investigation on its own"

title: DDA: a traceable multi-agent framework for automated structure-based drug design
authors: Yutao Yu; Sicheng Tian; Guohua Wang; Yang Li
task: turn a natural-language drug-discovery goal into an executed structure-based design workflow ending in a ranked candidate set
base_model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash for the production workflow at temperature 0.1, Qwen3-14B through Ollama fixed as the generation backend in the ablations, and GPT-5.2 used only as a temperature-zero rubric judge
tools_used: BioPython and docking utilities for target preparation, Fpocket for binding-site centres, RDKit and seed-construction scripts, the TamGen structure-conditioned generator, pandas, ADMET-AI property prediction, Uni-Dock and Vina-family docking, and viewers and a web front end for aggregation
evaluation_method: a fixed 100-target CrossDocked2020 test set with a twenty-candidate-per-target delivery contract, reporting drug-likeness, synthetic accessibility, docking score, diversity and a joint screen-pass rate, plus four controlled ablation suites on planning, tool selection, code execution and recovery
baseline: the specialised generators DiffSBDD, DecompDiff, Pocket2Mol and TargetDiff, matched raw TamGen controls with and without centre-guided localisation, and direct target-informed text-to-molecule prompting of GPT-5.2, Qwen3-14B and Llama 3.1
reported_result: 59.7% of delivered candidates passed the full multi-objective screen against 39.2% for the best specialised baseline and 7.8% for TargetDiff, with all 2,000 requested candidate records delivered while direct language-model baselines yielded valid docking scores for under 5% of the requested total
maturity_claimed: These results indicate that DDA provides a scalable, executable, and traceable computational framework that reduces manual coordination in structure-based automated drug discovery and delivers prioritized candidate sets with minimal human intervention.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the benchmark "uses reference-ligand-derived centers and computational proxy metrics" so "experimental binding, activity, selectivity, pharmacokinetic, and safety studies remain necessary before biological or clinical conclusions can be drawn", that the improvement "mainly comes from framework-level completion and filtering strategies rather than performance breakthroughs in the underlying generation model itself", that DDA "does not dominate every individual molecular descriptor", that the recovery outcomes "are assessments of recovery-plan quality under controlled declared states, not physical re-execution", and that a same-tool generic-agent baseline "will be an important future experiment"
code_availability: not stated as a URL; the release provides an environment template and non-sensitive configuration documentation, with further inquiries directed to the corresponding author

title: Autonomous Electromagnetic Simulation and Modeling of QFN Micro-Electronic Packages Using LLM Agents
authors: Hrvoje Molnar; Tvrtko Mandić; Vladimir Čeperić
task: build, simulate and reduce a quad-flat-no-lead package electromagnetic model from a natural-language prompt
base_model: not stated for the agent itself; the retrieval comparison tested Mistral 7B Instruct, Qwen3-14B, Qwerky-72B, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B, DeepSeek V3 and GPT 4.1
tools_used: PyAEDT scripts over Ansys HFSS for geometry creation, ports, solution setups, frequency sweeps, launching and monitoring solves and S-parameter export; scikit-rf for network analysis; an RLC fitting and SPICE netlist generator; and a FAISS vector index over HFSS documentation
evaluation_method: two experiments - a twenty-question binary pass/fail retrieval accuracy test across six models, and a comparison of the agent-generated twenty-pin package simulation against vector network analyser measurements from a prior study
baseline: none for the agent pipeline; the retrieval test compares six models against each other and the simulation is compared against measurement
reported_result: good agreement with measured data up to 1 gigahertz; the paper gives no headline numeric error metric in text, and states the approach "reduced the time and expertise required for package modeling from hours of manual work to minutes of natural language interaction"
maturity_claimed: The system successfully transforms user prompts into complete 3D models, executes electromagnetic simulations, extracts S-parameters, and synthesizes equivalent circuit models-all without manual intervention.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "the current model accuracy degrades above 1 GHz due to simplified geometric assumptions in the HFSS model" and that fixing it "will require implementing adaptive mesh refinement strategies and more sophisticated port modeling techniques"; that "the lumped RLC topology used in the paper is chosen as a proof of concept" and "The accuracy of more complex equivalent circuit topologies should be validated by measurements in an extended frequency range"; and that "the system currently relies on predefined geometric templates for QFN packages", so it performs "parameter optimization within fixed topologies" rather than "true design exploration". On the retrieval evaluation they add that "a more comprehensive evaluation procedure can be developed for deeper assessment"

title: Grid-Mind: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Fidelity Agent for Automated Connection Impact Assessment
authors: not stated
task: run an automated connection impact assessment for a generator or load interconnection request stated in natural language
base_model: DeepSeek-V3 for all reported end-to-end numbers, with Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen 2.5-72B supported at temperature zero and a cross-model pilot run for DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-4o
tools_used: eleven function-calling tools spanning backend and case management, power flow, optimal power flow, violation inspection, contingency analysis, impact assessment with and without mitigation, capacity search and network queries, over PandaPower, ANDES, ParaEMT and PSS/E

baseline: a cross-model pilot with DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-4o, the pre-clarification-gate baseline in the ambiguity recheck, and the ablated condition without the grounding layers; no non-language-model automation baseline

maturity_claimed: These results establish a reproducible baseline for continued refinement while maintaining auditable, simulation-grounded decision support.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that the transient and electromagnetic-transient acceptance criteria "are screening-oriented heuristics ... and do not constitute a replacement for utility-approved dynamic acceptance protocols", that "the evaluation does not yet constitute a blinded third-party benchmark", that "end-to-end numerical correctness validation against authoritative utility-grade reference studies ... has not yet been conducted", that the contingency threshold "is an implementation-specific parameter", that "the current mitigation action space is limited to shunt-like reactive compensation interventions", that "rigid pattern matching may fail to detect paraphrased or embedded numerical claims", and that memory may saturate the context window
code_availability: the scenario definitions, benchmark runner and timestamped result artifacts are stated to be in an accompanying repository, with no URL given

title: Aspen_Plus_MCP: an MCP server of typed schema-constrained tools over the Aspen Plus COM API
authors: EPEL-SNU
task: expose a chemical process simulator as typed Model Context Protocol tools so a local open-weight language model can interrogate, specify, build, run and cost a flowsheet
base_model: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ and an unnamed 14-billion-parameter open-weight model, served from a local OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint
tools_used: 42 typed MCP tools over the Aspen Plus COM API including stream and block reads and writes, a declarative flowsheet builder, a session restart tool and a techno-economic analysis tool, plus bridges onto external equation-oriented optimisation and costing packages that are not bundled
evaluation_method: a two-by-two harness comparing raw COM code generation against schema-constrained tool-calling on a roughly twenty-task suite over three bundled flowsheets, with an event log and an automatic failure taxonomy, plus an eight-prompt autonomous-synthesis bench verified by reopening the persisted artifact, a heterogeneous-routing experiment, a pre-registered ablation and costing validation

author_stated_limitations: the repository states that "the 14B cannot write a single working script in the 20-task suite (0/19 in the definitive run); the 32B manages 3-4/19", that "the precise limitation is *global spec correctness*, not 'ignores errors'", that one design task "is NOT auto-scorable - its expected (0.5) is the target stated in the prompt, so the model scored a false PASS", that semantic correctness is measured only on the simulator side, that "Aspen COM does not initialize over SSH", that the reported means come from small suites, and that "reliability costs tokens, not time"

title: mcp-solver: Model Context Protocol server for constraint solving (SAT, MaxSAT, SMT, CP, ASP, DP)

title: 24/7 Simulation Loops: How Agentic AI Keeps Subsurface Engineering Moving

tools_used: the OPM Flow reservoir simulator, in-house Python optimisation code implementing genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimisation, simulator APIs, database queries and retrieval over technical documentation and simulation manuals
evaluation_method: a single case study - well placement optimisation on the Brugge benchmark model, maximising net present value over 30 well locations - with a net-present-value convergence comparison of the baseline against the iterative agentic workflow
baseline: a non-agentic baseline optimisation run, not otherwise specified
reported_result: not stated numerically; the only quantitative anchor is a figure caption comparing net-present-value convergence and remaining oil distribution between the baseline and the iterative agentic workflow
maturity_claimed: The opportunity cost of inaction is now measurable. While traditional workflows wait in queues, agentic systems are already exploring the next iteration.
author_stated_limitations: none stated; the nearest qualifications are framing rather than limitation - that the assistant "is designed to augment, not replace, the established tools of the trade", and that integrating these capabilities into industry-standard high-fidelity platforms "represents an exciting evolution for the subsurface digital ecosystem"
code_availability: stated to be released as an open-source repository, with no URL given in the text

title: Automatic building energy model development and debugging using large language models agentic workflow
authors: NREL
task: generate and debug an error-free EnergyPlus input file from a natural-language building description

reported_result: all ten trials produced accurate and error-free input files, a 100% success rate, with the workflow completing the model in 9 minutes against 4 hours for an experienced modeller and two weeks for a student
maturity_claimed: The effectiveness of our workflow surpasses: 1) naive prompt engineering, 2) other LLM-based workflows, and 3) manual modeling, in terms of accuracy, reliability, and time efficiency.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "each case study begins with the assumption that the model geometry is already established", that "only HVAC templates were utilized", that "there is a lack of user interaction; the current model operates without further engagement with the user", that "a more comprehensive validation approach across more diverse buildings, modeling cases, and input scenarios would be needed", that "data privacy concerns must be addressed when employing commercial LLMs", that they "focused on two common error examples", and that "the Gemini model fails to successfully operate Agent 3, specifically in generating single objects correctly"

title: AGENTS4GEOS: agentic platform for open-source multi-physics simulation
authors: Adriano Cortês; Roberto M. Velho; Fernando A. Rochinha; Álvaro L. G. A. Coutinho; Mauricio Araya-Polo; Hervé Gross
task: build, run, diagnose and post-process multi-physics subsurface simulations from a natural-language request, and generate simulation ensembles for surrogate training
base_model: not stated by name; Claude Code is named as the harness, with capability-tiered routing that pins a mid-sized model for mesh and fluid computations and the most capable one for independent review
tools_used: 52 stateless MCP tools in six groups - schema introspection, fluid and constitutive properties, meshing, input-file assembly and validation, post-processing and preprocessing - built on an in-house schema engine, a fluid-property library, PyVista, an XML engine with a validator, and the ability to run the simulator itself and mine source PDFs
evaluation_method: one end-to-end session reproducing a published carbon-dioxide sequestration benchmark from a one-sentence request and comparing against the published figures, followed by generation of 200 parametric simulations validated against published results from two other simulators and used to train a graph-neural-network surrogate
baseline: published results from two established reservoir simulators and the source papers own figures
reported_result: a 500-year eight-well run completed in 2 minutes 49 seconds producing 101 reservoir snapshots, the whole session taking approximately one hour and 343,000 tokens with the user writing no input files and no shell commands, and 200 simulations generated for surrogate training
maturity_claimed: Agentic workflows like Agents4GEOS are transforming the accessibility of high-fidelity open-source simulation tools such as GEOS.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "meshing complex reservoirs is particularly challenging and warrants a dedicated specialized agent", that "more robust skill coverage is needed to ensure all simulations complete correctly", that "interacting with running simulations - monitoring convergence, diagnosing stalls, and steering or restarting runs mid-execution - remains an open direction", and that "token usage has emerged as a meaningful factor in the overall budget"; within the session they also record that the injection-rate tension "remains unreconciled in the sources", that the relative permeability "is an endpoint fit rather than the raw published curve", and that the saturation maps "used a density-based proxy"

title: EnergyPlus-MCP: A model-context-protocol server for ai-driven building energy modeling
authors: Li Han; Yujie Xu; Tianzhen Hong

reported_result: not stated numerically; the authors report only that the server "significantly reduces manual efforts while maintaining full simulation rigor", with the tool count of 35 the only figure specific to the system

author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "the current tool set focuses on model analysis and modification rather than complete model creation from scratch", that "the quality of AI-driven interactions heavily rely on the capabilities of the MCP client and the user's ability to formulate appropriate queries", that "users still need sufficient BEM knowledge to validate results", that "the protocol communication layer introduces minor computational overhead compared to direct EnergyPlus usage", and that "the server inherits any limitations present in the underlying EnergyPlus simulation engine"

title: Eppy-LLM: An Agentic Workflow for Language-Driven Building Energy Modeling And Optimization Using EnergyPlus
authors: Huiwen Zhou; Liang Zhang
task: turn a natural-language envelope design goal into parametric EnergyPlus runs and interpretable sensitivity feedback
base_model: a local instance of GPT-5 at temperature 0.2 for the parameter-reasoning agent; the other two agents are rule-based
tools_used: an input-file reading, editing, writing and syntax-validation library, the EnergyPlus 25-1-0 simulation engine, a typical-meteorological-year weather file and output parsing
evaluation_method: a single case study on the NREL iUnit model with three natural-language goals, producing nine modified input files plus a baseline run, measured on syntax-validation pass rate, repeat-run determinism over ten iterations, latency against manual scripting, and a top-five parameter sensitivity ranking
baseline: conventional manual batch scripting and the unmodified baseline input file; no competing agentic system
reported_result: every generated input variant passed syntax validation for a 100% correctness rate, with a median latency of about 10 seconds per iteration against roughly 30 seconds for manual batch scripting, and nine validated variants generated in 11.47 seconds
maturity_claimed: Applied to the NREL iUnit case study, the framework achieved end-to-end automation-from semantic goal interpretation to validated EnergyPlus execution-without manual intervention.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "the workflow depends on a pre-existing baseline IDF, assuming that building geometry and HVAC topology are already defined", which "restricts applicability in early-stage design", that the rule-based editor "may encounter parsing inefficiencies when applied to large commercial buildings with nested zones or intricate control sequences", that "semantic ambiguity in natural-language prompts can influence LLM interpretation", that "the current scope of evaluation metrics is limited to energy and comfort indicators", and that "minor variability can occur in the ordering of lower-ranked parameters across repeated runs"

title: MCP-enabled agentic AI workflow for building energy modelling: framework and use cases
authors: Han Li; Liang Zhang; Huiwen Zhou; Tianzhen Hong
task: compare two Model-Context-Protocol integration paradigms for driving EnergyPlus - conversational inspection and retrofit analysis against an autonomous agentic sensitivity workflow
base_model: GPT-5 for parameter schema construction and GPT-4o-mini for result interpretation and sensitivity analysis, with Claude Desktop as the client for the conversational paradigm
tools_used: the EnergyPlus-MCP server tools for file utilities, envelope management, input-file modification, retrofit management, simulation management, post-processing, output management and plotting, plus EnergyPlus itself and web search for code requirements
evaluation_method: two end-to-end demonstrations on the NREL iUnit model - a conversational retrofit study with practitioner-informed time estimates, and an agentic sensitivity workflow producing nine single-parameter variants, repeated ten times under identical inputs with token accounting and consistency checks
baseline: manual and traditional workflows estimated by practitioners and the unmodified baseline model; the authors state explicitly that the paper "does not attempt such quantitative benchmarking"
reported_result: an 80% to 90% time reduction for model inspection, modification and analysis, with the agentic workflow taking 9 to 12 minutes against about 2.5 hours manually; across 10 repeated runs mean 47,085 tokens (SD 7,912.1, min 34,793, max 63,120), split as 10 GPT-5 calls at 7,352.5 mean tokens and 85 GPT-4o-mini calls at 4,674.4; retrofit alternatives achieving 20.9% to 24.6% total energy savings; and the top-5 sensitivity ranking stable across runs at orientation 180 degrees 52.0%, orientation 90 degrees 18.1%, roof insulation thickness 7.0%
maturity_claimed: These demonstrations establish MCP as a foundational layer for AI-assisted building energy modelling, enabling natural language interactions with simulation tools while preserving professional oversight and decision-making authority.
author_stated_limitations: the authors state that "this work represents an early exploration rather than a production-ready solution", that the demonstrations "employed a relatively simple residential model with three thermal zones and ideal loads" so complex models "may pose different challenges that this study does not address", that language models "can produce incorrect tool invocations, misinterpret user intent, or generate plausible but inaccurate explanations", that with many tools available "the model may select inappropriate tools or become confused by overlapping functionalities, and LLM non-determinism means identical prompts may yield different tool sequences across sessions", and that "token consumption and API latency accumulate across extended sessions, making scripted approaches potentially more efficient for large-scale parametric studies"

title: Human–AI Teaming in Structural Analysis: A Model Context Protocol Approach for Explainable and Accurate Generative AI
authors: C. Ávila; Daniel Ilbay; David Rivera

evaluation_method: four case studies of three-dimensional frame structures, with outputs compared against conventional finite-element reference solutions and against unconstrained language-model answers, compliance checked against two national and international drift standards, and response time measured

reported_result: the abstract claims "deviations under 1.5% compared to reference" solutions; Table 9 reports GPT+MCP max-displacement relative errors against ETABS of 1.427%, 1.208%/1.624%, 2.834%/0.233% and 1.998%/1.422% across the four cases, so three of the eight case-direction pairs exceed 1.5%. Base shear (Table 10) is 0.007% to 0.022% and the building periods match OpenSees exactly. Standalone GPT without MCP reaches 235% to 482% max-displacement error and 27.8% to 43.6% base-shear error. Analysis cycles take 6 to 12 seconds

title: EngiAI: A Multi-Agent Framework and Benchmark Suite for LLM-Driven Engineering Design
authors: Gioele Molinari; Florian Felten; Soheyl Massoudi; Mark Fuge
task: benchmark and orchestrate multi-agent engineering-design workflows combining topology optimisation, retrieval and manufacturing preparation
tools_used: topology-optimisation and inverse-design problems from an engineering benchmark suite, a retrieval framework over a preprint index, web search, cluster job management over SSH, whitelisted local shell commands, and a 3D printer reached through a protocol server
evaluation_method: a three-part benchmark - a workflow benchmark of seven prompt styles, a retrieval benchmark with gated scoring, and a cluster benchmark of end-to-end model-training orchestration - across four model backends and two design problems, with fifteen runs per model-style cell

maturity_claimed: LLM-based multi-agent systems can reliably support structured engineering workflows when backed by sufficiently capable foundation models
author_stated_limitations: the authors state the benchmark problems "are limited to Beams2D and Photonics2D", that "only four LLM backends were tested, primarily due to API cost constraints", that the cluster training benchmark "covers only two generative models ... and two cloud LLM backends", that a user study with practising engineers was omitted, and that no single-agent baseline with identical tool access was run

title: Multi-Agentic Approach for History Matching of Oil Reservoirs

title: Multi-Agent LLMs for Adaptive Acquisition in Bayesian Optimization
authors: Andrea Carbonati

title: A generalizable automated geophysical agent workflow for accessible subsurface hydrology analysis
authors: Hang Chen
task: translate plain-language scientific intent into complete hydrogeophysical analysis pipelines - data loading, electrical-resistivity inversion, time-lapse inversion, multi-source data fusion, petrophysical conversion and reporting
base_model: GPT-4o-mini through the ChatGPT API, chosen for cost; the framework is described as also supporting other commercial APIs and local open-source models

author_stated_limitations: the author states that the fusion example "uses a sequential, structure-constrained inversion, while other joint or coupled inversion methods are not yet integrated", that "geophysics coverage is narrow, centered on ERT, seismic refraction, and basic climate linkage", that "the current uncertainty quantification propagates only petrophysical parameter uncertainty" so "survey errors, including electrode position uncertainty, reciprocal measurement errors, and temperature drift, are not yet incorporated", that "LLM hallucinations pose risks without stricter schema validation, tests, and version pinning", that "climate-resistivity links are correlational without modeling", and that "GAGAW is designed to augment, not replace, geophysical expertise"

title: Autonomous Flowsheet Synthesis, Simulation, and Analysis with a Locally Deployed Language Model Agent: An Open-Standard Interface to Aspen Plus
authors: Yeong Woo Son; Chan Kim; Ji Hun Pak; Dong Woo Kim; Kyoungmin Lee; Jong Min Lee

evaluation_method: 19 automatically scored tasks over three flowsheets in three difficulty tiers, run as a two-arm comparison of raw COM code generation against schema-constrained tool-calling at two model sizes, with the code-generation arm additionally run in an iterative variant that returns the execution error and traceback for up to three attempts; every attempt classified against a six-way outcome taxonomy

title: Multi-agentic AI framework for end-to-end atomistic simulations
authors: Aikaterini Vriza; Uma Kornu; Aditya Koneru; Henry Chan; Subramanian K. R. S. Sankaranarayanan
task: run end-to-end classical molecular-dynamics studies - structure generation, interatomic-potential retrieval, LAMMPS execution on HPC and property analysis - from a natural-language instruction

evaluation_method: six elemental and alloy systems (Fe BCC, Au FCC, Ni-Cu FCC, Ti HCP, Si diamond, Au-Cu FCC) across four task types - lattice constant and cohesive energy, elastic constants, phonon dispersion and melting point - with every agent result compared against a human expert given the same initial structure and the same potential file

The claim covering the wider crystal-system test is left as an unfilled placeholder in the published text: "The system achieved average errors below x% compared to the results of human LAMMPS simulation experts"

They also exclude potential choice from the agent's account: "the agent should not be held responsible for errors originating from the underlying potential choice"

title: Geo2UBEM: 3D Geometry Abstraction and LLM Multi-Agent Parameter Inference for Automated Urban Building Energy Modeling
authors: Wei Wu; Ming Qu; Zhe Wu; Yongfei Li
task: infer urban building energy-model parameters without metered data - reconstruct geometry from street-level imagery into EnergyPlus IDF, then drive a Bayesian optimisation loop against CBECS national median benchmarks until ASHRAE Guideline 14 convergence
tools_used: EnergyPlus 23.2 as the simulation engine, Optuna TPE for Bayesian optimisation (seed 42, 25 trials per pass, n_startup_trials 10, no pruner) with a process-isolated SQLite database per building, StreamVGGT reconstruction and RANSAC over street-level imagery, Microsoft Building Footprint and GIS references, and CBECS 2018 benchmark tables
evaluation_method: six calibrated campus buildings of four types at Purdue University (101,170 square metres) in climate zone 5A, calibrated meter-free against CBECS 2018 medians and then validated independently against actual metered EUIs from Purdue Facilities Management; a three-layer sensitivity and uncertainty analysis (Morris screening, Sobol decomposition, Monte Carlo propagation) was run alongside
baseline: the neutral-parameter Phase 1 baseline IDF, and conventional metered-data calibration workflows described but not re-run; independent validation against actual metered EUIs
reported_result: ASHRAE-consistent convergence on all six buildings (|NMBE| <= 5%, CV(RMSE) <= 15%) with no metered input; final NMBE from -1.22% (University Hall) to +1.04% (MSEE); four buildings converged in a single LLM-MAS iteration, PMU Club in three and MSEE in seven; average inference cost $0.09 per building, under $0.55 for the campaign; equipment density accounts for 80-99% of annual energy-use variance while envelope parameters contribute negligibly (Sobol S_T <= 0.005)
maturity_claimed: Geo2UBEM achieves ASHRAE-consistent convergence (|NMBE| <= 5%; CV(RMSE) <= 15%) without any metered input, a result not previously demonstrated for a multi-building cohort
author_stated_limitations: the authors list seven, among them that "Six buildings in a single climate zone (CZ5A) constrain statistical representativeness"; that "Ideal-loads systems reduce modelling uncertainty but suppress equipment-level dynamics"; that "LLM reasoning is externally hosted and cannot be fully reproduced across model versions"; and that "Hardware scalability is extrapolated beyond the observed workload" - projecting six-building parallelism linearly "has not been validated at larger scale". They also name "upstream geometry quality control and reproducible pipeline orchestration" as "the two most manual components in the current workflow"
